Stepping up to the mike, the CM welcomed the crowd to the temple, which he described as a "gorgeous *āśrama.*" He told the attentive audience, "It is not far from the truth to say that there is no place like this in our world." He lauded ISKCON and glorified Śrīla Prabhupāda personally for reviving temple construction, temple worship, *Gītā-parāyana*, and for disseminating Vedic culture to what he called "advanced countries like the U.S.A." His spoke for about ten minutes, finishing with a request that everyone take full advantage of the facility ISKCON is providing.

Mr. Raju then spoke, followed by Muthyal Rao. Mr. Rao addressed the crowd in Hindi, giving another strong personal endorsement. "We are very fortunate that Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda, a very elevated personality, opened this temple with the generous donations of so many generous people, especially Mr. G. Pulla Reddy. If they had not given this place, we could not have this temple. Therefore I am indebted to all of those people who have helped in this temple."

Declaring himself an avid reader of *Bhagavad-gītā*, he enthusiastically lectured the crowd, at times sounding like an apocalyptic fundamentalist preacher as he warned his audience to devote their time to hearing the words of great saintly persons before impending destruction, or *pralaya*, overtook India. "We should. ... meditate on those words, not that we hear from one ear and let it out from the other, that is not *puṇya* \[piety\]. Just like the Chief Minister said, that we Indians, we are taking to their \[Westerners\] way of life, they to ours. He said that we are losing our intelligence. I really feel that days of *pralaya* are coming near. It is very bad, very bad, *dharma pralaya*. Therefore I request you all that when a saintly person comes to preach among us we should take his teaching to our hearts and do some service to the humanity. And we should not deviate from *bhakti-mārga*.

"*Bhakti* has become a joke these days. If I started wearing saffron cloth or chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa, the whole world will laugh at me; therefore please do not make fun of *bhakti*, do not make fun of God. This is very sinful. When someone preaches about absolute truth, both the speaker and the listener get the benefit; in the same way, when someone blasphemes, both the speaker and the listener get bad reaction, sinful.

"On this auspicious day I congratulate the Chief Minister and everybody who has come here today and also special congratulations to Swamijī. I have a special respect for Swamijī. So many ministers, Chief Ministers, come and go but their words always remain with us. In the same way these saintly persons preaching will always remain with us, their name always remains in the hearts of people, their good deeds always remain with us.

"I have some special relationship with Swamijī. I have been watching him with all his Western disciples. One of his disciples came and said to me, 'I have come from sinful *bhūmi* \[the West\] to speak to the people of *puṇya-bhūmi*.' I was completely overwhelmed. So please try to understand *Bhagavad-gītā*, read it everyday. We are expert singing cinema songs. I also do that, I also play sitar, but I also read *Bhagavad-gītā* and I am proud of it. Therefore please start reading *Bhagavad-gītā*. You all just come and have *darśana* and offer your respects. That is not enough, but also try to elevate yourself more. Like one goes to Tirupati and chants *'Jaya* Govinda, Govinda Govinda,' and then leaves. Become more devoted.

"I am glad that Swamijī graced my house yesterday. He always comes whenever he comes to Hyderabad. I thank everyone who has come to attend this function. A lot more people should come."

In Śrīla Prabhupāda's keynote address he spoke on *Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam* [1.7.6](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/7.6). He told his audience that the literary contribution of Vyāsadeva is not possible for anyone else to repeat in any age, and that of all the literatures presented by Vyāsadeva, the *Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam* is the spotless *purāṇa*, free of any cheating. In it, *bhakti* is established as the stage beyond liberation. Although some may claim otherwise, Śrīla Prabhupāda emphasized that that is not the opinion of *śāstra*. He told the crowd, "It is a misconception that *bhakti* helps *mokṣa*. *Brahma-bhūtaḥ prasannātmā.* Without Brahman realization, *ahaṁ brahmāsmi*, there cannot be jubilation, *prasannātma.*"

He said that because *bhakti* is enacted on the liberated platform, the Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement may therefore be a little difficult to understand. He quoted *Bhagavad-gītā* [7.3](https://vedarama.com/en/books/bg/7.3) and said, "We understand superficially, 'Kṛṣṇa was born in Mathurā, and He was the son of Vasudeva, and so on, so on.' But one has to understand Kṛṣṇa, *tattvataḥ*, in truth. And Kṛṣṇa says *janma karma ca me divyaṁ yo jānāti tattvataḥ. Tyaktvā dehaṁ punar janma naiti*, if you understand simply Kṛṣṇa, *tattvataḥ*, then immediately you become liberated."

Mr. Rao had stressed that everyone should read the *Bhagavad-gītā*, and so did Śrīla Prabhupāda. "We are missing our own culture that we do not take very much care to understand *Bhagavad-gītā* as it is. We make our wrong interpretation and spoil the whole thing. These habits should be stopped, otherwise our culture is almost already lost. Then this *bhāratīya* culture, it is very important culture. Caitanya Mahāprabhu has said that, *para-upakāra*. The *bhārata-bhūmi* is meant for doing good to others. *Bhārata-bhūmi* is not meant for exploiting others. That is Caitanya Mahāprabhu's mission. Because every Indian is born Kṛṣṇa conscious, naturally he has got instinct. Don't destroy it. Don't destroy it. That is our request ... If we simply introduce this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement, you'll very soon see that the face of India is different."

Because he was following Kṛṣṇa's direction he said that Kṛṣṇa consciousness was successfully spreading all over the world, modestly referring to his hard labor of the last eleven years as "only a teeny and humble attempt."

As he repeatedly does, he urged one and all to participate in their culture, in the spirit of Lord Caitanya. "So if one man could do, if you say, some success, why not all of us? Caitanya Mahāprabhu has given power of attorney to all Indians, *bhārata-bhūmite haila manuṣya-janma yāra*. He's speaking to the *manuṣya*, not to the cats and dogs. First of all, try to understand what is the purpose of life. That is called *janma sārthaka*. Go. Everywhere there is very good demand for Kṛṣṇa consciousness. So everyone should be prepared, everyone should understand *Bhagavad-gītā*. Of course, it is not possible for everyone to go—still, if one understands, that is also Caitanya Mahāprabhu's order, *āmāra ājñāya guru hañā tāra' ei deśa*. He says everyone of you become a guru. Even though you are not very much educated or not born of a very high family, you simply *yāre dekha tāre kaha kṛṣṇa-upadeśa* That's all. Don't adulterate it, but as Kṛṣṇa says, you say. You become guru.

"So I have tried that. I have tried to follow the Caitanya Mahāprabhu's instruction, and I am presenting *Bhagavad-gītā As It Is*. There is no magic, there is no jugglery and people are taking. If you do that everyone will be happy, the world will be happy and India's glory will be spread all over the world.

"Thank you very much."

His lecture finished, Śrīla Prabhupāda dismounted the *vyāsāsana* and went with his guests to the front of the Deity room for the first *darśana* and *ārati*. The temple room was packed with eager visitors, all pushing and straining so as not miss the sight of Their Lordships.

We waited—and we waited. Our *pūjārīs* were struggling to get everything ready, but finally, with the help of Sampath Kumar Bhaṭṭācārya and his fellow Bangalore *brāhmaṇas*, they opened the doors at 12:15 p.m. With a great cheer the crowd surged forward. The priests blew three long blasts on their conches, announcing the imminent appearance of the Supreme Lord and His eternal associates. Then the curtains opened to reveal the splendorous forms of Their Lordships Śrī Śrī Rādhā Madana-Mohana, Śrī Śrī Gaur-Nitāi, and Śrī Śrī Jagannātha, Baladeva and Subhadrā. All were beautifully dressed, and the crowd pressed forward yet again while our devotees chanted in an ecstatic *kīrtana*.

Śrīla Prabhupāda, appearing well-satisfied with the ceremonies, remained with his guests at the front until the end of the *ārati*. Then the Chief Minister and other guests took their leave and Śrīla Prabhupāda returned to his rooms, where he stayed for the rest of the day.

But the temple room remained crowded the entire afternoon as people patiently received their packets of *prasādam* and awaited the next *ārati*. At about 5:30 p.m. most of the devotees went out on a *harināma* parade through the city. An elephant led the procession, carrying the small Gaura-Nitāi deities. Even when the parade left, the temple stayed three-quarters full, but there was no program to keep the guests engaged. Seeing this I took the initiative and, without formally asking permission from Śrīla Prabhupāda, who was still napping, I went down to chant over the microphone. As the time for the evening *ārati* grew near a few hundred more people appeared, so I also gave short talk on the benefits of chanting Hare Kṛṣṇa.

The parade returned at 6:45 p.m. and after another energetic *ārati* the devotees asked the crowd to sit while they chanted *bhajanas*. During the chanting Mahāṁsa came to Śrīla Prabhupāda's room and requested him to sit out on his balcony and benedict the crowd with his *darśana*.

Prabhupāda was happy to oblige. We hastily set a padded cotton mattress on the little overhang and Prabhupāda sat there, high up in the temple room, chanting along with the devotees and encouraging the crowd to join in. The fact that the balcony still lacked a railing turned into an advantage because His Divine Grace could easily be seen by all. He stayed out there for about twenty minutes and threw flowers down to the crowd. When the *bhajana* ended, Śrīla Prabhupāda returned inside, and the enthralled audience was then shown the film *Spiritual Frontier*.

\* \* \*

In the late evening Śrīla Prabhupāda asked Pālikā to cook *ekādaśī-prasādam*. She served it to him around 10:45 p.m. We were all amazed that he had managed to complete the fast.

Just before he took rest at 11:15 p.m. it began to pour with rain. Watching from his window as the heavens opened up, Prabhupāda smiled contentedly and said it was an auspicious sign that everything had been a success.

It was difficult for him to rest, however, because of the noise coming from the huge crowd that had gathered for the midnight *ārati*. As it turned out, *ārati* wasn't actually held until 12:40 a.m., but everyone waited patiently and stayed on for the feast afterwards.

## August 19th, 1976

Today is Śrī Vyāsa-pūjā day, the 80th birth anniversary of Śrīla Prabhupāda. We are all fasting for half a day but unfortunately Śrīla Prabhupāda is also practically having to fast. He has bad digestion and is coughing up a lot of mucus. He had only a very small amount of fruit for breakfast and simply *khichari* and yogurt for lunch.

As soon as I got up this morning I thought about what to offer him. Puṣṭa Kṛṣṇa Swami had written a Vyāsapūjā offering as Prabhupāda's secretary that is included in the Vyāsapūjā book. But I was not aware that I could have also done the same, so there is nothing from me in it. I thought that perhaps I should try to do something special for His Divine Grace, but then I thought it might interfere with my regular service. And anyway, I am already serving Śrīla Prabhupāda twenty-four hours a day so it doesn't seem that I can do much more than that. After some internal debate I have decided to just press on with my normal service in a spirit of full surrender and hope he will be pleased with that and accept it as my offering.

\* \* \*

Prabhupāda received Gargamuni and Jayapatāka Swamis for a brief moment in his room before taking his breakfast. They had just arrived from Māyāpur and Prabhupāda was pleased to see them. Right away he informed them that his health was not good. Gargamuni said he knew this and, to Prabhupāda's satisfaction, he produced some medicine Prabhupāda had asked his sister for some time ago.

Since the Bengali Communist Party seems to have been the source of the recent propaganda against us, Prabhupāda was pleased when the *sannyāsīs* showed him a favorable article which was published in the *Ananda Bazaar Patrika*, a Calcutta newspaper with a circulation of about 500,000. Prabhupāda said that gradually people all over the world would appreciate his movement.

Particularly interested to hear that Bhavānanda Mahārāja had invited the members of the Communist Party of India (CPI) to come and visit Māyāpur, Prabhupāda asked what was their reaction.

Gargamuni answered that they were a little bit envious because Māyāpur is becoming very popular amongst the local people. "We get 5,000 now for the *prasādam*. And even the Congress leaders, they come and eat with the people. They said, 'This is wonderful.'"

Prabhupāda was pleased to hear that Jayapatāka Swami has been traveling in the villages, selling up to 700 *Gītār-gānas* a day. He was even happier when he heard that all the publicity this was generating was attracting more and more people to come and visit our temple.

Because of the special programs scheduled for his Vyāsapūjā, Prabhupāda asked the *sannyāsīs* to give him a more detailed report in the afternoon.

\* \* \*

The devotees held *kīrtana* in the temple room in anticipation of the moment when His Divine Grace would come down and join them. It was a rare opportunity to be able to worship him in person on the day that we all revere more than any other of the year. At 11:00 a.m. they all leaped, danced and shouted as he took his place on the half-finished marble *vyāsāsana*. The GBCs and *sannyāsīs* stepped forward to wash his feet while Sampath Kumar Bhaṭṭācārya and his Bangalore contingent chanted various *mantras* in praise of him. Yaśodānandana Swami led us in *guru-pūjā* and then *puṣpāñjali*, the offering of flowers. He chanted aloud Śrīla Prabhupāda's *praṇāma mantras* three times as we responded, and then, with a culminating cry of "*svāhā*! *svāhā*! *svāhā*!" we showered handfuls of flower petals at Prabhupāda's lotus feet and bowed our heads in joyful obeisance.

These ceremonies completed, Prabhupāda asked Harikeśa Mahārāja to read from the Vyāsapūjā book. He stood at the microphone and read out the submissions of Tamal Krishna Goswami, Brahmānanda Swami and Gopāla Kṛṣṇa prabhu, and then allowed Śrī Sampath Kumar Bhaṭṭācārya to step forward to the mike and make his own extemporaneous offering.

Sampath Kumar was an animated speaker, punctuating his words with rhythmic chants as he enthusiastically lauded Śrīla Prabhupāda and his movement. The audience clapped several times as he glorified His Divine Grace for reviving and spreading Vedic culture all around the world.

Then, on Prabhupāda's request, Harikeśa got up again. This time Prabhupāda had him read out the names of every ISKCON center in the book. He wanted to impress upon the large gathering of people the strength of the ISKCON movement and its acceptance all around the world.

When Gargamuni Mahārāja took his turn, he included in his glorification some extremely favorable book reviews, gleaned by the members of the Library Party he manages, from professors here in India. Śrīla Prabhupāda was especially pleased to hear these.

Jayapatāka Swami completed the eulogies, emphasizing how Śrīla Prabhupāda was successfully defeating the Māyāvādīs and impersonalists by preaching the glories of Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Person. He said that his achievements were the proof that Śrīla Prabhupāda is directly empowered by the Lord Himself, and that anyone seeking a bona-fide spiritual master in order to find their way out of material entanglement and attain Kṛṣṇa *premā*, should know that there is no better guide than Śrīla Prabhupāda. "Although he is before us," he concluded, "we cannot understand his greatness. Neither we can estimate it by our minds or intelligence. But we must know for certain that his mercy and his power is unlimited because he has fully dedicated himself under the lotus feet of Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa.

"Therefore we call him 'Prabhupāda' because he is the pure representative of Prabhu; and therefore he is deserving of the title 'Prabhupāda.' And with great honor and pride we are pleased to address His Divine Grace as 'Śrīla Prabhupāda.'"

Then Śrīla Prabhupāda spoke. Given the number of guests present, he explained first why he occupied his impressive throne-like seat. He said there were two reasons; the *vyāsāsana* means the seat of Vyāsa, which the representative of Vyāsa is allowed to sit on; and *vyāsa-pūjā*, the worship offered to the representative of Vyāsa on his birthday.

He went on to lucidly describe the importance of the guru. "Now I must explain my position because in these days, a person being worshiped as most exalted personality is something revolution. Because they like democracy, by vote somebody should be elevated however rascal he may be. But our this system, *guru-paramparā* system, is different. Our system, if you do not accept the Vedic knowledge through *guru-paramparā* system, it is useless."

That acceptance he said, meant presenting things as they are given in the *Vedas* even though they may appear contradictory. He described how the stool of an ordinary animal is contaminated and, if touched, one has to immediately take a bath, but that according to the *Vedas*, the stool of the cow is pure and is used in the performance of sacrifice. "So it appears contradictory, the Vedic injunction. But still we accept because it is Vedic order. That is the acceptance of *Vedas*. Just like *Bhagavad-gītā*. *Bhagavad-gītā*, there are so many rascals, they cut short: 'I like this; I do not like this.' No. Arjuna says *sarvam etad ṛtaṁ manye*. That is understanding of *Vedas*. If a rascal makes cut, cutting, 'I do not like this, I interpret,' this is not *Bhagavad-gītā*. *Bhagavad-gītā* means you have to accept as it is. That is *Bhagavad-gītā*. We are presenting therefore *Bhagavad-gītā As It Is*. ... Anyone who does not come through this *paramparā* system, if he presents any interpretation of Vedic literature, it is useless. It has no meaning. *Yogo naṣṭaḥ parantapa.* You cannot interpret on the words of God."

He said that to accept Kṛṣṇa means to accept His representative. "Somebody may envy that this person has sophisticated some disciples and they are offering prayers and *pūjā*. No, it is the system. Don't envy the ... *Ācāryaṁ māṁ vijānīyān nāvamanyeta karhicit*. *Ācārya* is the representative of God. *Yasya prasādād bhagavat-prasādo*. If you offer prayers, honor to the *ācārya*, then Kṛṣṇa the Supreme Personality of Godhead is pleased. To please Him you have to please His representative. 'If you love me, love my dog.'"

Prabhupāda said that although Kṛṣṇa Himself says that the *ācārya* should be accepted as Himself, still, an observer may think, "Why? I see that he is a man. His sons call him father, or he looks like a man, so why he should be as good as God? Because he speaks as God speaks, that's all. He does not make any change."

As to why one should accept a guru, he said that since the world is full of rascals, it requires many gurus to teach them the science of the spirit soul and thus deliver them. Informing his admirers and inquisitive onlookers that a guru is not a magician, he humbly submitted his claim as our guru and invited them to emulate his work according to their capacity. "So practically I have done this. People are giving me credit that I have done miracles, but my miracle is that I carried the message of Caitanya Mahāprabhu: *yāre dekha tāre kaha 'kṛṣṇa'-upadeśa*. So this is the secrecy. So anyone of you, you can become guru. It is not that I am an extraordinary man, an extraordinary god coming from some mysterious place. It is not that—it is very simple thing. So I request you follow the Caitanya Mahāprabhu's instruction that you also, you become a guru at your home. It is not that you have to make a gigantic show of becoming guru. The father has to become guru, the mother has to become guru."

He concluded with a sincere and humble request. "Vedic culture means by the evolutionary process we come to this human form of life. Here is the chance of stopping transmigration of the soul from one body to another. Civilization is *punar janma jayayaḥ*, how to conquer over next material birth. That is this Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement. Therefore we are presenting so many literatures. It is being accepted all over the world, learned circle. Take advantage of this movement. We have tried our humble attempt to open a center here. Do not be envious upon us. Kindly take mercy upon us. We are making our humble attempt. And take advantage of it. That is our request."

To cheers and applause Śrīla Prabhupāda gracefully stepped down from the *vyāsāsana*, thanked Sampath Kumar and his men for their attendance and support, and then returned to his room as the devotees conducted an enthusiastic *kīrtana*.

\* \* \*

With two of the Indian zonal GBCs here there was a discussion about a disturbing report that some so-called devotees presently visiting India are dealing in drugs. They claim that because they give some of the proceeds for various ISKCON projects their behavior is justified. They reason that if something is used in Kṛṣṇa's service it transcends ordinary morality and becomes purified. More disturbing still is the report that some of our Society's leaders are tacitly approving such behavior by accepting donations from these men, knowing that the funds were earned by illicit means. Harikeśa Mahārāja brought it to Prabhupāda's attention in Bombay and, needless to say, Śrīla Prabhupāda is very disturbed by this warping of our philosophy.

Today, with Prabhupāda's approval, Harikeśa Swami drafted a letter, later countersigned by Gargamuni and Gopāla Kṛṣṇa, to be sent to all GBCs warning them not to have any contact with these people. "It has come to His Divine Grace's attention that many members of our society are engaged in the same business that Rsabhadeva (ex-President Laguna Beach) and devotees of Laguna Beach Temple were engaged in. ... His Divine Grace is very, very unhappy about this. He said that under no circumstances can any GBC or Temple President accept any money from these devotees. This business has to be stopped at once immediately. His Divine Grace wants all of you to refer to the instruction of 3rd verse of Upadesamrta. First and foremost our profession must be very honest—above all suspicion. His Divine Grace said 'I am trying to retire from management to translate but if these things come then how can I translate. I have set up the framework and everything should be done within the framework. Kindly see that this business is stopped at once.'"

\* \* \*

After massage, *prasādam* and rest Śrīla Prabhupāda happily met with his two Bengal-based *sannyāsīs* at 4:00 p.m.

Jayapatāka Mahārāja has been working earnestly since the last festival in order to get government authorization for the acquisition of about 350 acres of land for the Māyāpur project. Mr. Choudhuri, the gentleman from the planning department Śrīla Prabhupāda met in New Delhi airport last December, has been a great help in this endeavor. Jayapatāka and Gargamuni said that overall the reaction has been favorable, although there have been some ups and downs. They outlined what has been a tentative course of events.

Our plans had gone through all the lower departments, but then about a month ago they received a negative response from Siddhanta Shankaraya, the Chief Minister (CM) of Bengal. He told Jayapatāka, "I would have refused this application except for the impassioned appeal of one of my senior officers, namely Mr. Choudhuri. They are asking for 300 acres of land but the East India Company, they asked only twenty acres of land and they ruled India for 200 years."

Śrīla Prabhupāda raised his eyebrows a little. He commented that the rule of the East India Company was political. "Even if we are rule," he said, "we shall rule spiritually. We have nothing to do with politics."

Gargamuni said even the Chief Secretary thought the CM's comment was frivolous. Still, the CM had not blocked the application but he had requested further investigation of our Society. "We showed them the handloom; we showed them the *gośālā*; we showed them the children. Even Tarun Kanti Ghosh, he came, and we lined up fifty children, and they read the *Gītār-gāna*, and he almost started crying. He liked it so much. He said, 'Oh, you have done so nicely with the children.' So they were impressed with the work."

Tarun Kanti Ghosh, the Home Minister, personally contacted the CM, and as a result, the CM decided to let Mr. Choudhuri make the decision. But Choudhuri was hesitant. He told Jayapatāka, "I cannot simply take the decision. They'll say I am biased. I must work in the ordinary ways of the government. But there is no trouble now. You have waited so long; wait another 60 days, and then you'll get it."

Then a few days ago Jayapatāka contacted Mr. Choudhuri to invite him for Janmāṣṭamī. "I asked him what the \[news was\]. He said he had recently received a phone call from the Chief Secretary—'You see? Now your favorite project is going to be spoiled.'"

Jayapatāka said Mr. Choudhuri had gone to see the Chief Secretary, who showed him an article how the question had been raised in the Rajya-Sabha whether ISKCON was linked with the CIA or not. "Then Mr. Choudhuri said, 'Sir, I am not afraid.' He said, 'Why not?' 'Because I have you, don't I?' Then the Chief said, 'Yes. You have won me over. I believe in this project.'"

However, despite the Chief Minister's approval, Jayapatāka said that Mr. Choudhuri didn't want to take the full brunt of the decision on himself. Mr. Choudhuri wanted the Nadia District Planning Committee to make the decision. "So the head of the Nadia District Planning Committee is that minister, Anandamoy Visvas. So I went to him and I gave him an invitation for the Janmāṣṭamī. So I showed him that letter where you have said that 'every day we're selling $60,000 of books, and I thank you for helping me.' I said, 'Sir, we are simply doing Prabhupāda's order. This is not our work. It is not a foreign work. It is his work; we are simply doing it. He is selling so many books that he wants to invest some of the money to develop Mahāprabhu's birthsite. That is all. He has got the money. Why he should not invest it?' He said, 'I am going to have a meeting of the committee next week, and I'm going to push your project through. We're going to pass it.' That is the last word I heard. So it looks that everything is very good right now. But we have to keep our society very pure because they are investigating us very strong. All the time they're having people watching us."

Gargamuni said that right now some special advisors to the Prime Minister are in Māyāpura investigating us and Jayapatāka added, "Some of the local people that were working with me, getting petitions, they came and told me that some people from Delhi or outside were inquiring about us, about Bhavānanda Goswami, about Jayapatāka, about this project, about how the devotees are dealing with the public, whether we are doing any anti-Indian work. All sorts of questions they are asking. So it's very important that we keep very up and up right now. All the time. But otherwise the government, they are happy with our work. And so far, Mr. Choudhuri said, other people have indicated that they have found no bad report about our society, although they are looking so hard. Therefore they are passing."

Gargamuni explained that although the local and State government is favorable, the central government doubts our intentions because they don't know us.

Jayapatāka added that the local police intelligence officer has told him that his application to become an Indian citizen, now under consideration for about a year, will definitely be accepted.

Śrīla Prabhupāda was satisfied to hear their report on the government. He asked, "What about our Godbrothers? They are also opposing?"

Jayapatāka said that even if Prabhupāda's Godbrothers were against us, they had no power to influence things. He also said that seventy percent of the local people are favorable to the scheme with the other thirty percent doubtful and perhaps only one percent actively opposed. Even a local Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) who was formerly opposed to our project, is now offering to help us.

He said that everyone appreciates our work, especially our free food distribution. Recently the price of rice went up by about 80 paise, and as a consequence the number of recipients of our weekend food distribution has increased from 1,200 to over 2,000 per day.

Gargamuni said that the only downside of the investigations was that collections from wealthy people in Calcutta has decreased because people were a little afraid that if they gave to us, they may also be investigated. The income tax department is conducting vigorous raids on the wealthy, resulting sometimes in confiscation of money and land. But Gargamuni felt this was a minor obstacle. When Prabhupāda said that it sounded like our program was going on, he assured Prabhupāda that it was increasing.

"That I want," Prabhupāda smiled.

Having brought Śrīla Prabhupāda up to date on the acquisition, the two *sannyāsīs* then discussed a suitable spot for building Śrīla Prabhupāda's house. It is scheduled to be built next to the *pukkur*, the small lake near the main entrance. But Gargamuni said that spot is noisy because we have 138 residents now, 50 of them children, living in the rooms on the front wall. Prabhupāda agreed with Jayapatāka that the decision could be made after the acquisition goes through.

Last March Prabhupāda had asked that the large panels sculpted in cement along the front wall be painted with advertisements for his books. He was satisfied to hear that two artists, Ānakadundubhi and Pāṇḍu prabhus, have completed about seventeen of them.

Jayapatāka was positive in his assessment of the Haridaspur project, which he was given charge of after Prabhupāda's visit there last March. Although the land is still not signed over to us yet, since there are fourteen members of a family that have to sign, nine in Haridaspur and the rest in Calcutta, he didn't think there would be any problem. He also thinks that the funds required for development of it can be raised in the local neighborhood from wealthy families. He expressed confidence that the whole village could become Kṛṣṇa consciousness if someone was there to work with them.

Prabhupāda agreed and told him, "Chanting is the main thing. Chanting and distributing *prasādam*."

As we talked, Prabhupāda sent for Pālikā and instructed her to make a potato and tomato *subji* for this evening. He also asked that she prepare a light *khichari* for his breakfast tomorrow. His digestion is still not good, but he hopes the medicine the *sannyāsīs* have brought will help.

That done, he turned his attention back to the report, expressing concern about the immigration department. He said his disciples are making big arrangements but if they are refused visas and forced to go away then who will manage everything.

Both Gargamuni and Jayapatāka said they had no real visa problems; they simply had to keep going in and out every six months. But Śrīla Prabhupāda encouraged them to find some means to secure their status, otherwise he said it would be like Alexander the Great—as soon as he was absent from his kingdom, everything was finished.

They suggested that Śrīla Prabhupāda write a letter to the Home Minister, explaining that all of ISKCON'S activities are actually being done by Śrīla Prabhupāda, and his foreign disciples are simply assisting him.

Prabhupāda agree that that was actually the fact, and indeed he has already sent a letter like that.

In trying to encourage Śrīla Prabhupāda to come to Māyāpur, Gargamuni said that the monsoon this year was mild. But Śrīla Prabhupāda wasn't impressed. "I have got bad impression, Bengal during rainy season."

When I offered that that was perhaps on account of all the insects that season brings, Prabhupāda shook his head. The insects were not so bad, he said; it was more because of his indigestion.

Gargamuni asked whether any part of India was good during the rainy season and Jayapatāka added that he personally only knew Bengal.

Prabhupāda laughed. "You are now Bengali," he declared, and then asked for further details on Jayapatāka's application for Indian citizenship.

Jayapatāka explained that it had been bounced back and forth between Māyāpur, Calcutta and Delhi several times, and then he was re-investigated. "At that time they brought in some local people, and one investigator, he said that 'This Jayapatāka Swami, we have heard that he is a very bad person. He beats the people.' They said, 'No, We never heard such thing.' 'No, no. We have heard that he is very bad.' In this way by negative they are testing. They came and told me that for two hours police is drilling three different people from Navadvīpa and Māyāpur. In this way no one said a bad..."

Prabhupāda smiled. "No, if you are a famous man, then they'll do."

"Now Bhavānanda is more famous," Jayapatāka said.

Prabhupāda grinned. "He is notorious."

"But now he is in the papers," Jayapatāka added.

Prabhupāda laughed, shaking his head at the foolishness of our critics. "You are famous; he is notorious. It is very difficult to deal with these nonsense. They are devotees and neither notorious or famous."

Musing on the increasing level of recognition his disciples are getting, Prabhupāda added, "Our Godbrothers, they do not like Bhavānanda. Eh?"

Jayapatāka agreed. "No. They don't like me any more either."

When Prabhupāda asked why, Jayapatāka explained their psychology. "They always thought, because I am not so outspoken, that 'Jayapatāka, we can get him to do as we like.' But ultimately I don't do anything for them either, so now they don't like me either. Bhavānanda was openly against, and I was passive. I didn't say anything." He said that recently he had rejected an invitation from Madhava Mahārāja to attend a festival because he was afraid of being poisoned. "If not materially by poison, then spiritually by ear. One way or another they have to give poison."

Prabhupāda agreed that was their business.

Jayapatāka also relayed the news that Bhakti Vilasa Tīrtha Mahārāja, head of the Śrī Caitanya Gaudiya Matha, is now on his death bed. "He can't breath. He is on a bed with oxygen. Life and death any moment. Injection, oxygen, barely staying alive. One day better, one day worse. In this way his life is going on." He added that Tīrtha's brother, Sambidānanda, who is a barrister, was reportedly preparing to take *sannyāsa* so that he could take over the running of the Matha.

Prabhupāda noted the news with noncommittal silence.

The two *sannyāsīs* gave an encouraging report on the development of our Māyāpur Candrodaya Mandir, stressing that persons of a higher calibre, who are sincere to improve spiritually by attending all the programs, were now being attracted.

Prabhupāda nodded agreeably, "Yes, it may not be the association of lazy people, free hotel. No."

Gargamuni said that Bhavānanda Mahārāja was strict. "Without working, no one can eat."

"Not only working, attending the program," Śrīla Prabhupāda said. "That is essential."

Prabhupāda inquired whether they were producing sufficient cloth from the hand looms to meet all their own needs and encouraged them to sell any excess to the foreign temples.

Before they took their leave, Jayapatāka Mahārāja asked for Prabhupāda's views on our western men marrying Indian girls.

Prabhupāda said he has no objection but said the problem is the men will not stay, either in India, or in the marriage. So from that perspective, he advised against it.

By this time the *kīrtana* from the 4:30 p.m. *ārati* in the temple was booming and reverberating throughout the room. It made discussion difficult so the *sannyāsīs* finished their report and left, with a promise to return tomorrow.

## August 20th, 1976

Construction continues even as the temple functions move into full swing. There is a constant banging and clatter, but Śrīla Prabhupāda doesn't seem to mind; he is happy to see the work being done, and is pleased with the opening. Many local people are attending the *āratis*. Even the neighborhood children have found a new haven to frequent, eagerly chanting with our devotees and taking *prasādam.*

\* \* \*

After the hectic schedule of the past few days Śrīla Prabhupāda finally got some time to deal with his mail today. He began by dictating a note of thanks to Sampath Kumar Bhaṭṭācārya and the Bangalore *brāhmaṇas*, who are leaving tomorrow. After complementing them on conducting the *yajñas* so nicely, he reminded Sampath Kumar that in Kali-yuga the real *yajña* is *harināma saṅkīrtana*. He finished with a request that they help spread Kṛṣṇa conscious brahminical culture all over the world.

The Sydney temple president, Jayadharma dāsa, wrote reporting that they had distributed 15,000 sweet balls at their recent Ratha-yātrā. He also requested initiation for Mark Phillips and his wife Jane. Mark wrote to Śrīla Prabhupāda last December asking for guidance, and Prabhupāda advised him to move into our temple. He took Prabhupāda's advice and so was now receiving the name Mahotsaha dāsa. His wife is to be called Jagat-priya dāsī.

Trivikrama Mahārāja wrote, outlining a plan to remain in the West until he has sufficient funds for his preaching in Taiwan.

Prabhupāda liked the idea. "Do it. This is a very good program. This is a very gentlemanly idea. Unless one has an office and a sitting place, no one really cares about you."

\* \* \*

Jayapatāka Mahārāja, and a little later, Gargamuni Swami, returned to see Śrīla Prabhupāda during his midday massage. The sounds of construction—sawing, banging and the chip-chipping of hammer and chisel—and the low clamor of visitors in the temple room were ever-present in the background, yet Prabhupāda sat on a straw mat in his *gamchā* as I smeared mustard oil on his body, giving full attention to Jayapatāka's report.

Jayapatāka said that due to Prabhupāda's expressed desire to develop other holy spots, he has been taking the opportunity to visit various places mentioned in *Caitanya-caritāmṛta* as he toured Bengal.

Not far from the mango grove Prabhupāda stops at for breakfast whenever he goes to Māyāpur, in the village of Pālapāḍā, and about one mile south of the Cākadaha railway station, is a temple with the same Gaura-Nitāi Deities that Maheśa Paṇḍita worshiped. There are also several other Deities and a dozen *śālagrāma-śilās*. Maheśa Paṇḍita is described as the seventeenth branch of Lord Nityānanda and the seventh of the twelve *gopālas*. The current *sevait*, Śrī Keshav Priya Brahmacārī, is a disciple of a former British World War I air pilot called Richard Nixon. Nixon settled in Almora in the Himalayas and was later initiated as Krishna Prem by one of the Gosvāmīs from the Rādhā-Ramaṇa temple.

Keshav Priya wants to give the temple to ISKCON. It is well developed and maintained and Jayapatāka said that the man appears to be a competent manager. He holds an annual festival that attracts several thousand pilgrims.

Prabhupāda nodded in approval.

Another property that may be offered to us is the original house of Rāghava Paṇḍita at Pānihāṭī. According to Tarun Kanti Ghosh, the committee in charge of the house recently decided to offer us the *sevā* there.

Unconcerned that it is in a dilapidated state, Prabhupāda told Jayapatāka to take it; it can be repaired. He is happy at these offers but he did, however, sound a note caution. "Difficulty is that if we take charge, we may give it for worshipping to one disciple, but the immigration department will gag him. That is the difficulty. And we don't have many Indian disciples. Otherwise we can take all these important places."

Estimating that each foreign devotee has to leave and then return at a cost of 10,000 rupees, he said, "If that 10,000 rupees was invested in developing that center, much improvement could be done. But they are gagging. They are dreaming, 'CIA.' You can bring so many men and keep everyone in charge of such places, and it will develop. Money, there is no scarcity. But the difficulty is that as soon as we establish, the immigration, 'You go away.' Otherwise there is no difficulty. We can take all the charge and develop them very nicely. So if one man is kept in charge, and after a few months he's advised, 'Go away,' then all his training goes to hell and we have to spend another 10,000 rupees."

He told Jayapatāka to explain to the authorities that "Prabhupāda has put this philosophy: *andha-paṅgu-nyāya* \[the blind and lame working cooperatively together\] ... Let American money and India's culture combine together and the whole world will be benefited. Convince them. It is not a question of India, America—it is a cultural movement for the benefit of the whole world."

He told Jayapatāka to appeal to the devotional sentiments of Tarun Kanti Ghosh. "'So Tarun Babu, you are such a devotee of Caitanya, Caitanya Mahāprabhu wants it. Why don't you help us? Your family is devotee of Lord Caitanya, and this is spreading Caitanya's mission. You should give up everything and join this movement if you are actually a devotee of Caitanya. And Prabhupāda says that he knows at your heart you want that Caitanya's movement is spread all over the world, so far he has studied you. So let us join together. Why we should unnecessarily be biased, American and Indian? Everyone will be happy. India will be glorified; America will be glorified. If within ten years we have got so much success, if we work continually, the whole world will be...'"

Prabhupāda gave Jayapatāka the go-ahead to accept any offers of historical places.

They went on to discuss life membership and Śrīla Prabhupāda gave instructions on what benefits may be given. He said there should be no misunderstandings, as there have been in the past. He advised them to give five books on loan to each member, and then when they have read these five, they can exchange them for five more. He stressed that it should be made clear that only three days free lodging at a time is allowed. "In the future they may not complain, as they are doing. Somebody is coming, 'Oh, we have given 1100 rupees to live forever.' Some ladies came like that. They take it, advantage, 'Oh, we shall get books and live forever. There is no charge.' That misunderstanding should be cleared up."

He was referring to a woman who had turned up in Vṛndāvana last year claiming that her life membership entitled her to free board and lodging in our guest house for the rest of her life. The dispute was only settled when Śrīla Prabhupāda personally intervened. If someone wants to live like the devotees, Prabhupāda said that they may be allowed to purchase a room and we will supply free *prasādam*, but they must attend *ārati* and follow the rules and regulations.

Gargamuni described that a wealthy Maḍwari man from Calcutta was offering us fifteen acres of agricultural land and a large marble house near Beekanair in Rajasthan. Prabhupāda said to take it, but Gargamuni said he was reluctant because we already have such a huge property in Māyāpur.

But Prabhupāda quoted an old saying, "If somebody offers you very nicely washed cloth, you should use it. And some property, you must use it." He said that people are rotting outside of Kṛṣṇa consciousness and we should help them to develop their spiritual lives. "This is combination of rich man, poor men, for Kṛṣṇa. The same, *andha-paṅgu-nyāya*. Both of them are useless separately, and when they combine in Kṛṣṇa consciousness they are all useful.... So our propaganda is, 'They are separately planning useless. Let them combine together in Kṛṣṇa consciousness. All this planning shall be successful."

Jayapatāka smiled appreciatively. "We were all useless in the West, but you have come and then engaged us."

Śrīla Prabhupāda took his praise humbly. "It is Kṛṣṇa's desire. Nobody is useless. I was also useless. I could not do in India alone anything." He chuckled. "Two useless makes useful; intelligence alone cannot work, money is required. A man may have very good brain power, organization, but if he has no money—useless. So four things required: land, labor, capital, organization."

He referred to his recent meetings with the Endowments Minister and their discussions about what to do with the funds which are donated to Balajī at Tirupati. "He is inclined to spend huge income of Tirupati for Kṛṣṇa consciousness. But he is bound up by other colleagues. They are applying the money. So he is willing to call all the ministers if I can convince them. I shall try it."

He explained the spiritual considerations in the giving and utilization of money. "The *karmīs*, the village cultivators or big men, industrialists, they are going to Tirupati. Whatever they can spare, they are offering. That is *yajñarthe*. If this money is taken and again if it is brought into *karmī*, then it is misleading. Just like people are giving us money. They are *karmīs*. But because they are giving us and we are engaging the money in Kṛṣṇa consciousness so the money is fully utilized. But if this money is taken and again to the *karmīs*, then it is a farce. His purpose is served \[the giver\], but one who is misleading, he becomes criminal. He is to be punished.

"Suppose in our Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement somebody gives us money. He is giving in good faith that 'It is very good organization.' But if I misspend that money, then I am responsible; then I'll be punished. His business is finished—Kṛṣṇa noted that he has given his hard-earned money for spreading Kṛṣṇa consciousness. If I take that money, instead of doing Kṛṣṇa consciousness, if I use it for my sense gratification, then I will be responsible.

"What is the use of Kṛṣṇa's money being used in industry? Any purpose outside Kṛṣṇa consciousness ... Let this money be utilized for spreading the glories of Kṛṣṇa. But they do not recognize Kṛṣṇa. All the so-called *Bhagavad-gītā* readers, they want to kill Kṛṣṇa."

Reporting on the situation in our Calcutta temple, Jayapatāka and Gargamuni told Prabhupāda that Abhirām, the president, tried to obtain permission from the local authority to build a temple in the center of the lake in the park across the road. The Calcutta Corporation at first were not inclined, but the Minister of Municipal Affairs liked the idea. The obstacle, however, is that although they will allow us to build a monument to Śrīla Prabhupāda, they will not allow any Deity to be installed.

Śrīla Prabhupāda quickly informed them how to get around that. "Well, then take this proposal: 'All right, no Deity, we shall hold meetings, lecture.' What is that? In the park people come, and we decorate the whole hall with pictures. Gradually we worship one picture."

Jayapatāka said Mr. Choudhuri similarly suggested that we bring the Deity once a week, and simply hold *kīrtana* at other times. He thought that in this way the Deity can gradually stay for a week, then a month....

Śrīla Prabhupāda liked that idea as he is eager to see the project come about, considering it the best spot in Calcutta. And from a philosophical and practical view point, it was appealing to both ends of the political spectrum. "Anyone can come to the park. Convince them. 'Come on! Take *prasādam* sumptuously.' They'll be satisfied. They are hungry. Actually they are hungry, poorly paid, capitalist and worker. The trouble is, capitalists, they are taking all the profit, and they are enjoying life in wine and women. Naturally the worker will see that, 'Why we are working so hard and they are making profit, and they are enjoying, and we do not live in a very nice house? It is a slum.' Naturally they will be envious. If the capitalists spend the money for Kṛṣṇa consciousness—in each and every factory they hold festivals and give them eatables like anything, everything will be successful."

Gargamuni Mahārāja saw the possibilities for our collections to increase and he grinned. "We tell them that, 'If you give your Kṛṣṇa tax, this will save you from the income tax.' Because they are raiding ... because 'You are hoarding. But if you give...'"

Prabhupāda was nodding. "Yes, yes. The industrialists ... That is also one of our programs. Let them hold festivals every Sunday, as we hold. And we shall go and have *kīrtana* and sumptuous feeding give. They'll be very satisfied. And instead of giving the income tax, let them spend in this way. Convince them."

Gargamuni stressed that 3C Albert Road was in adequate for our needs, and besides, we continually have difficulties with our landlord.

Prabhupāda asked whether the house on the corner of the lake that he had inspected in late March could be purchased but Gargamuni said the owner didn't want to sell.

It was clear that Śrīla Prabhupāda wants to do something wonderful in Calcutta. He even suggested that we try for the famous Victoria Memorial. He said it was not being utilized nor properly maintained but if we had it, Kṛṣṇa would maintain everything.

Jayapatāka grinned, seeing the irony of such a proposal. "And we could have British *pūjārīs,* for the glory of Queen Victoria."

Prabhupāda smiled. "Tell them that we shall bring ... to worship Victoria with *prasādam* of Caitanya Mahāprabhu. That is real Victoria Memorial."

As the meeting drew to a close, they discussed establishing a bank in Māyāpur. So far only a local cultivators' financial cooperative has shown interest, but Prabhupāda doesn't want to deal with them as they want a large deposit from ISKCON. "If you deposit five *lakhs* now, it will decrease value in five, ten months. The purchasing power of money is decreasing. Now what you can purchase with five *lakhs* of rupees, after five years you'll require ten *lakhs*. So your money will decrease. And if you invest that money in land, after five years it will increase to its full extent. So why should we waste our money? What is the benefit?"

Gargamuni pointed out that the farmers don't usually keep their money in the banks, although now the government is trying to force them to do it.

Prabhupāda was well aware of what was going on. Because farmers traditionally use their money to buy land, the government has declared a land "ceiling," a limit on what one individual can own. "So they cannot invest money in the land; they give to the bank. And as soon as you keep money in the bank it will decrease the value. Money is decreased, value of, all over the world. Because it is not money actually, it is paper, cheating; real money is gold. But they will not allow to keep the gold. The whole policy is vicious. If I purchase gold with five *lakhs* of rupees, then it is real money, and after five years I can sell it ten *lakhs*. That they will not allow.

"Therefore my policy is that whatever money is there, spend; don't keep; in land and produce food. That is the best use. And instead of keeping money and take interest, you print books. That is also good, you can sell. Or you purchase land for producing food."

Gargamuni had a good grasp of the principle. "If we stock money, then there'll be no preaching. But if we print books, then we have to sell the books. So that is preaching."

"Therefore I am insisting all over," Prabhupāda said. "Print any book. Never mind either Hindi or English or ... Print book and keep it in stock, nicely. That is the purpose of my Bhaktivedanta Trust. Fifty percent must be spent for printing, and fifty percent for building. That's all. No money. Don't keep any account."

"Then the government will never get envious because there's nothing there," Gargamuni added.

Prabhupāda agreed. "Yes. And we haven't got to keep so many accountant, auditors, and other nonsense, unnecessary things. As soon as there is collection, invest the money in some building or in making some book, book printing. Follow this policy. I am very much eager. I have got money here and there, but I want to spend it in this way. So therefore I am advising take this. We shall invest renovating them and in developing them. Spend money. Don't keep money." He described how food prices are increasing at a greater rate than the interest paid on a bank deposit. So if we print books and sell them at 100% profit, no bank can give such a return for the investment.

"Your books will be our bank," Gargamuni said.

"Yes. We have got business. Why shall I keep in the bank?" Prabhupāda concluded. "This is the policy: if your money is idle, we can spend it in our books, in our purchasing land in temple, constructing temple, developing."

\* \* \*

In the evening Prabhupāda gave a short *darśana.* There was some discussion about whether Śrīla Prabhupāda should visit Mahabaleshwar, a hill station near Poona, where one of our Bombay members, Mr. Malhotra, has offered land and a house. Prabhupāda was considering going there when we leave here on the 25th, but Mr. Panilal Pithi, a life member with whom Prabhupāda had stayed in March 1975, advised him to wait. He said it was not a good idea at this time of year as some 300 inches of rain has fallen during the monsoon. So Prabhupāda decided that he will go to Delhi as previously arranged and he will visit Mahabaleshwar later in the year.

## August 21st, 1976

Ekādaśī. Prabhupāda had only a small bowl of milk and a separate bowl of tapioca for his breakfast, and for lunch, a simple meal of *kutta-atta paratha,* a potato and a fruit salad.

\* \* \*

Śrīla Prabhupāda called us in early, at about 5:00 a.m., and complained quite strongly that he could not translate during the whole of the night because a dog in one of the neighboring houses was howling and whining. He said we should lodge an official complaint to the police that the owners are mistreating the animal.

\* \* \*

Sampath Kumar Bhaṭṭācārya and his men came up to Prabhupāda's room to bid him good-bye. They expressed great happiness with the installation and considered it an honor to have been invited to conduct the ceremonies.

Equally appreciative of them, Śrīla Prabhupāda urged them to sustain this spirit of cooperation and help spread Kṛṣṇa consciousness to the world. He happily posed for a photograph with them and he accepted a gift of a *śālagrāma-śilā* from Sampath Kumar before they left.

\* \* \*

Saurabha prabhu arrived from Bombay last night and Śrīla Prabhupāda eagerly heard from him and Gopāla Kṛṣṇa prabhu as he took his massage. Prabhupāda was keen to know about the Janmāṣṭamī festival, especially since a preliminary report suggested that only 600 guests had attended.

Saurabha assured him that the festival had been a big success, and he estimated at least 20,000 visitors came over the two-day period. He said that people had crammed in everywhere, even sitting on the unfinished balconies and the scaffolding.

Referring to the low estimate, Prabhupāda wanted to know where it had come from. "Who is that nonsense who came and said this? Who is that rascal?"

Gopāla Kṛṣṇa sheepishly revealed that it was a thirteen-year-old boy.

Prabhupāda shook his head in mild disgust. "Oh. You believe the boy? He's authority. Here is the authority, you take the information. How did you believe the boy?"

So pleased was Śrīla Prabhupāda with Saurabha's news that he offered the Bombay temple the *śālagrāma-śilā* Sampath Kumar had just given. *Śālagrāma-śilā* is already being worshipped in Māyāpur and now the Bombay temple is becoming well established he has decided to expand the worship.

Saurabha informed Śrīla Prabhupāda that construction had resumed and was proceeding quickly. They are now putting up the walls of Prabhupāda's quarters. He unfolded the plans to show Prabhupāda the layout. Prabhupāda's sitting room will be about 32 feet square and there is a bedroom, secretary and servant's rooms, plus a kitchen and reception. There will also be a room on the roof for Śrīla Prabhupāda to enjoy the open air and fresh sea breezes. Śrīla Prabhupāda seemed very pleased with them.

Saurabha went over other details of temple and guest house facility. Provision has been made for a bank at the front entrance. Several of the bigger banks are interested, and Prabhupāda told Saurabha to go with whoever offers the best rate per square foot.

All the other construction is moving ahead. The second floor slab of the temple is being cast, and in one more month, they will lay the main slab of the *darśana-maṇḍapa*; after that they will start building the domes. Saurabha explained that the domes will be made from precast rings of reinforced concrete, stacked one on top of the other; if it works here, he will probably use the same method for the Māyāpur temple construction. The tiling work has already begun in the Deity basement and Saurabha was confident of the overall progress. "So they guaranteed that at the end of this year the building—that means the guest house—will be completed. And of course, that includes the temple. The only thing which will definitely go on is the marble work, the carving; that is a very big job. But that we can always continue—that is mainly outside work, finishing—so that we get the inside ready for the opening."

Śrīla Prabhupāda was satisfied, both with the progress report and Saurabha. He asked him if he had checked the Hyderabad temple.

"I have not gone around, but it looks very nice," Saurabha told him.

Prabhupāda smiled. "It is after your design," he reminded him.

"Yes," Saurabha acknowledged. "But I haven't been in Hyderabad for at least eight months."

Prabhupāda assured him. "They have done nice."

Saurabha wondered whether he should begin to develop the plans for Māyāpur since Jayapatāka Swami had told him the acquisition would come through within two months.

Śrīla Prabhupāda told him to wait until the sanction is actually given. He said unless the government gives the land it may be difficult for us to get everything we need because of all the opposition. "If we remain Kṛṣṇa conscious Vaiṣṇavas, then our position is strong," he said. "If there is slackness, then they will come to kill us. That we have to see. *Āpani ācari' prabhu jīve śikhāilā*. Our behavior should be very clear. 'Caesar's wife must be above suspicion.' Then it will be all right."

Prabhupāda said that there will always be people trying to disturb this movement, just as various demons like Aghāsura and Bakāsura came to disturb Kṛṣṇa. He reminded us of a Bombay film producer who made a film in which he depicted the devotees as drug-addicted hippies. "That Devananda, 'Hare Kṛṣṇa film,' he wanted to do some harm. And he is gone, finished. Nobody talks of Devananda, they talk of our movement. So if you remain strong in your spiritual activities, these Aghāsura, Bakāsura we don't care for. But we should take precaution and counteract to reduce them. Real strength will remain from Kṛṣṇa-Balarāma's strength. Balarāma. Balarāma means strength. *Nāyam ātmā bala-hīnena labhyo*. If you are not supported by Balarāma, then it is not possible. So we have got our Balarāma, Kṛṣṇa-Balarāma temple. Now in Europe we have got Kṛṣṇa-Balarāma."

Describing New Māyāpur in France, Prabhupāda told Saurabha and Gargamuni, "Nitāi-Gaura and Balarāma. *Brajendra-nandana jei kṛṣṇa, śaci-suta haila sei:* 'He is now Śacī-suta.' *Balarāma haila nitāi:* 'And Balarāma has become Nitāi.' That's all. These two brothers. And devotees are very nice, 200 devotees there are. And they are taking *prasādam* on the open lawn—very nice. Presently they are growing vegetables sufficient for their consumption and for the Paris temple. Fresh, nice vegetables. Flowers, grains also they have got. Barley and wheat. Milk also—their own cows. So if there is milk, there is food grain, there is vegetable, so what do you want more? Enough we can grow. They have got 200 acres of land, some portion of the land they are utilizing. That is becoming sufficient for them. And if they grow the whole land, they can make good trade. Just like in Philadelphia they are producing so much milk, they are selling outside $1,500 per month."

Prabhupāda meant our farm in Port Royal, Pennsylvania. He praised its president, Paramānanda, describing him as "very expert" and, fondly recalling the *capātīs* cooked for him by Paramānanda's wife, Satyabhāmā dāsī, he gave a broad grin. "When she brought, it was so thick. And, 'How shall I eat this?' But when I ate, it was so nice, soft and sweet. I ate everything."

Despite the grand plans and huge projects he is developing, Prabhupāda's reflections of his recent tour revealed that his ambitions for his Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement are really quite simple and modest. "All the boys and girls are very happy. So that I want, that I live happily and chant Hare Kṛṣṇa. That's all. We don't want unnecessary luxury. *Anartha-nivṛttiḥ syāt*. *Anartha* should be reduced, nil-bare necessities. *Anartha* ... Just like this material thing we require for preaching. That is not *anartha*. But when it is used for sense gratification, that is *anartha*. Anything for sense gratification, that is unwanted, *anartha*. And anything for Kṛṣṇa consciousness, that is spiritual. *Ānukūlyena kṛṣṇānuśīlanam*. So whatever we are using, that is not material. It is all spiritual."

Prabhupāda also discussed with Saurabha the proposed gift of land in Mahabaleshwar. Although Prabhupāda stuck to his decision not go there until at least October, Saurabha's description of the place was so appealing that Prabhupāda told him to go ahead and accept it.

Gopāla Kṛṣṇa explained that the donor, Mr. Malhotra, wanted Prabhupāda to decide after seeing it personally.

But Prabhupāda said, "We shall go in October. So when Saurabha has seen, that is my seeing."

Gopāla Kṛṣṇa said Mr. Malhotra's only condition was that he wanted us to actually develop it.

Śrīla Prabhupāda enthusiastically said he was willing to spend several *lakhs* of rupees there. He said residential quarters could be built and the householders from Bombay could live there.

\* \* \*

After Saurabha, Gargamuni and Gopāla Kṛṣṇa left, Mahāṁsa came in to inform Śrīla Prabhupāda that the door for his balcony was finally completed and would be fitted while he took his bath.

Mahāṁsa Swami is a soft-spoken, mild-mannered fellow, and Prabhupāda smiled after he went out. As I finished his massage he commented to me that Mahāṁsa was doing nicely. I offered that he was very sincere, and Prabhupāda agreed. "Everyone likes him. He has no enemy. Nobody has complained against him."

I said, "He's very even-tempered."

Prabhupāda chuckled. "Neither he has complained against anybody. He does not complain, and nobody complains against him." He added that Mahāṁsa's mother had been very sorry that he had joined us, but now she is very happy.

\* \* \*

A low-class, tabloid-style newspaper called *Blitz*, has just published a disparaging article about us. Under the heading "The Ungodly Face of the Krishna Cult," the *Blitz* editors have attempted to impose sinister intent into our activities here in India. So after Prabhupāda got up from his post-lunch nap and we had given him some fresh fruit juice and a newly-made flower garland, he met with Jayapatāka, Gopāla Kṛṣṇa, Gargamuni and Pradyumna in order to formulate a response.

The article gave an overview of our projects here, deliberately slanting the facts with fallacious detail meant to fuel the speculation of our supposed CIA connections.

Śrīla Prabhupāda was not passive about the matter. As he listened to Pradyumna read out the article, he told Gopāla Kṛṣṇa to sue the *Blitz* for $50,000 for their libelous accusations.

But at the same time he retained his sense of humor. Hearing their description of our Bombay property—"In point, in Bombay, a huge plot was acquired in Juhu for rupees fourteen *lakhs*. They have put up a temple there with a barbed wire fence around it"—Prabhupāda said, "Yes, the barbed wire is there. No *Blitz* editor can go there!" We laughed as he added, "No dogs and *Blitz* editors allowed!" He told Gopāla to include this in his response to them.

Every description of our activities was warped in someway or other. Pradyumna read on. "This is completely nonsense: 'Their major concentration seems, however, to be in Orissa the land of princes and paupers. They have built a center close to our atomic energy commission complex.'"

Jayapatāka Mahārāja pointed out that the "major complex" was simply Gaura Govinda Mahārāja living in a few brick and thatched huts.

The piece went on trying to paint us as political subversives. "They reportedly met also our deputy defense minister, J. B. Patnayak, who hails from Orissa. It is understood that Patnayak has asked the district magistrate of Purī to find land for ISKCON's Sanskrit university there. ISKCON is pursuing not only Kṛṣṇa, it has started taking interest in politics also. It has founded a political party in the United States called 'In God We Trust' Party. It has already contested civic elections in Los Angeles and intends to put up candidates for the U.S. Congress."

Prabhupāda didn't have a problem with that. "What is wrong there? In God We Trust, this party. Yes."

"They are making it sound as if it is a political party," Gopāla Kṛṣṇa explained. "They're saying we're using God as a front."

"They may say," Prabhupāda asserted. "But we want to put forward a God's party also. Why not? Everyone is godless party. We must push forward a God's party. What is the wrong there? Our whole movement is to educate this atheistic godless civilization to God consciousness. That is our movement. So if we set up a party, In God We Trust, what is the wrong there? We are trying to elevate the demoralized human society to God consciousness."

The newspaper has somehow managed to obtain internal ISKCON correspondence, citing a letter Prabhupāda wrote from Hawaii to the GBC in May: "Now we've become more than the British Empire. Even the British Empire was not as expansive as we are. They had only a portion of the world, and we have not completed expanding. We must expand more and more unlimitedly."

Prabhupāda had a ready answer. "You also explain, that British Empire expanded by military strength, and we are expanding by Ratha-yātrā. We are expanding our empire simply by Ratha-yātrā."

I paraphrased a headline that had been in the New York Times. "East meets West."

"Singing, dancing and chanting," Pradyumna added.

"Yes," Śrīla Prabhupāda smiled. "We introduce three chariots in big, big cities and conquered them."

I reminded Śrīla Prabhupāda of a London newspaper headline about our Ratha-yātrā. Śrīla Prabhupāda nodded. "They admitted: 'Rival to Nelson's Column,' in *Guardian* even. So who is strong enough? We are stronger than British Empire. Simply by Ratha-yātrā we are conquering, and actually that is being done. What I have got strength? Forty rupees beginning. Simply Hare Kṛṣṇa and Ratha-yātrā, that's all. That's a fact."

The article continued with its dark hints that we were up to no good. "The Indian government has been rather slow in picking up the ISKCON signals. One reason being that the genuine Krishna devotees in the administration had been mighty pleased in the beginning with the idea of exporting Krishna consciousness to America."

It stated that initially action had been taken against allowing foreign devotees to stay in 1971, but that in 1975 the Home Ministry had taken a more lenient view "on the specious plea that the mastering of Vaishnava literature, the spiritual diet of the cultists, was not like learning shorthand."

Then, under the heading "Contrary Pulls in Government," the article referred to the current controversy in the central government. "Lately, of course, the center has become wise, though contrary pulls in the thinking process still persist."

Prabhupāda was dismissive of their attempt to blacken our name. "This article, no sane man will take notice of it. No sane man will like. It is not very important article." Still he said we should bring them into court. He asked his GBCs, "But what will be your charges?"

"Defamation of our religious cult," Gargamuni suggested. "Because we're recognized by scholars as being bona fide. It says here, 'Ungodly face of Krishna cult.' How is that ungodly?"

"Yes, this is the charge," Prabhupāda said. "That very heading is a defamation, 'Ungodly face of Krishna cult.' This is the charge, others are subordinate. This is the main charge. We are spreading Kṛṣṇa, God, and he's 'Ungodly face.' Minimizing the value of the movement."

As it happens, the *Blitz* offices are in the same building as our lawyer, Mr. Asnani, so Prabhupāda told Gopāla Kṛṣṇa to immediately send him a letter and begin proceedings. "So prepare a case for these rascals. We have got strong case. And charge, 'Why you have made "ungodly"? Prove it. What do you know about godly?' Charge them. So there will be discussion, long discussion, what is godly and what is not godly. Put them in the corner. 'What do you know, rascal, about godly tradition?' Then it will be exposed. Do, immediately do. Immediately plan to bring in the court."

This article renewed our fears that perhaps there may be attempts to interfere with Prabhupāda personally. He again agreed, as he had in Bombay, that perhaps he should remain in one place and have a proper guard.

Having settled the course of action to be taken against *Blitz*, Prabhupāda turned to Pradyumna prabhu. He asked him if would like to personally worship the *śālagrāma-śilā* given by Sampath Kumar, which was still sitting on his desk. He obviously had changed his mind about sending the Lord to the Bombay temple.

Pradyumna was readily agreeable and so Prabhupāda gave him some simple instructions. "So we can carry, and every morning just put in a *siṁhāsana* and *tulasī* and water and flower and little fruit. That's all." Then turning to the rest of us he said, "He has got tendency to worship."

"He is *brāhmaṇa*, *paṇḍita*," Gargamuni added.

"Paṇḍitjī," Prabhupāda smiled, calling Pradyumna by his popular sobriquet.

Gargamuni mentioned that Pradyumna was also training his son, Aniruddha, and Prabhupāda smilingly added, "Yes, his son will be great *paṇḍita*. Both of them are devotees—husband and wife; therefore nice son is born. *Yathā bījaṁ yathā yoni*. *Yoni* is the mother, *bījam* is the father."

Then Prabhupāda digressed a little, fondly recalling how his own father, following the advice of his spiritual master, always traveled with *śālagrāma-śilā* hanging around his neck wrapped in a linen handkerchief. "Yes. So it is safe always, *kaṇṭha*. My father used to carry. Wherever he would stay, *gaṅga-jala*, *tulasī*, decoration; say, half an hour business. My father was a great devotee, yes."

"You dedicated the *Kṛṣṇa* book to him," Gopāla Kṛṣṇa recollected.

Śrīla Prabhupāda smiled. "Yes. Because he was a pure Vaiṣṇava. And he wanted me to become like this. He was praying to Rādhārāṇī. And any saintly person would come, he would simply say, 'Give blessings to my son that he may become a Rādhārāṇī's servant.' That was my father's prayer. He never prayed that 'My son may become very rich man.' He never prayed like that. Actually, his ardent desire that his son may become a Vaiṣṇava and my Guru Mahārāja's training, has put me this position. That I have admitted, later on. What is that word I have given? Hmm? Find out."

Gopāla Kṛṣṇa knew just what Prabhupāda meant. He quoted, "Which was later on solidified by my eternal father."

Prabhupāda's eyes lit up. "Ahh! Read it."

Gargamuni read Śrīla Prabhupāda's dedication from the front of the *Kṛṣṇa* book: "To my father, Gour Mohan De, 1849-1930, pure devotee of Kṛṣṇa, who raised me as a Kṛṣṇa conscious child from the beginning of my life. In my boyhood ages he instructed me how to play the *mṛdaṅga*. He gave me Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa *vigraha* to worship and he gave me Jagannātha Ratha to duly observe the festival as my childhood play. He was kind to me, and I imbibed from him the ideas later on solidified by my spiritual master, the eternal father."

As we expressed our appreciation, Prabhupāda's features softened with natural humility and affection. "That is a fact. I got good father and good spiritual master."

Gargamuni contrasted that with our fortune. "We have gotten bad father, but now we have spiritual father."

But Prabhupāda didn't agree. "No bad father. Unless good father, son cannot be good. *Yathā yoni yathā bījam*." He added that his father had never chastised him.

I thought I remembered him saying that his mother was always very strict and I mentioned this.

Prabhupāda smiled. "Because he was very lenient; so mother had to be little strict for my education."

As the meeting broke up and everyone filed out, Prabhupāda finalized Pradyumna's new duty with him. He told him to buy a small *siṁhāsana,* a *pañca-pātra* waterpot, and some fine linen from which he should make a small *dhotī* and *chadar* for the Lord. He was to worship Him with flowers, *tulasī* and *gopī-candana*. He referred him to the painting in *Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi-līlā*, where Śrī Advaitācārya was depicted worshipping the *śālagrāma-śilā,* and told him to follow that example.

He instructed Pradyumna, "First thing is that when you take *śālagrāma-sevā*, wherever you stay, this worship must go on daily. That you cannot stop. One day, if you are sick, your wife will do that. But that half an hour *pūjā* must continue. That you must decide. So both of you are initiated. In case you are little sick, your wife will do. In that platform you have to do it. *Sevā* shall not be stopped. Gradually as your son grows, he will also do it."

So although Prabhupāda sometimes complains about Pradyumna's *smārta-brāhmaṇa* tendencies (he once said that he had saved Pradyumna from becoming a *smārta*) still he recognizes his good brahminical qualifications and learning and is always encouraging him to develop them.

Just before we left his room, Prabhupāda referred to the newspaper and parliamentary commotions. "Anyway, now they are feeling the weight. That is the progress. Otherwise, if our movement would have been a trifle thing, the government and newspapers they would not have taken care. Now they are feeling that this movement is going to be more and more important, all over the world.

\* \* \*

Jayapatāka Swami had a final *darśana* of His Divine Grace this evening before departing back to Calcutta. Along with Gargamuni Mahārāja, he heard from Śrīla Prabhupāda of the pro-active stance he is taking against all the false propaganda. Prabhupāda informed them of a letter he is writing to Mr. Channa Reddy, one of the state Governors. "I'm writing one letter to the governor that I work hard, I print my books and they are selling. And if I bring the money to construct temple, why people are envious? What is the wrong there? Rather, I should be encouraged that I am bringing so much money in India, foreign exchange, by my very, very hard labor. So why they are envious?"

Gargamuni Mahārāja said he felt it was difficult for them to believe that a *sādhu* could possess so much money from selling books.

"That may be beyond their dream," Prabhupāda said, "but I am not so-called *sādhu*. I am trying to execute the orders of my Guru Mahārāja, predecessor. I am not a so-called *sādhu*, taking a saffron robe, begging for fulfilling the belly."

"They have to accept you as an international leader," Gargamuni said.

"I must be international leader," Prabhupāda agreed as a matter of fact, adding that such huge sales of a single person's books, especially philosophical and religious works, was unique in history. He laughed and said that the public generally considered such literature untouchable. Thus, his feat is even more remarkable.

Observing that the Māyāvādī, Vivekananda, produced only one small booklet: "Thus Spake ... ," and that two of his own leading Godbrothers, Bon and Tīrtha Mahārājas, have not been able to produce any substantial literature, Prabhupāda said they were *chalas*, bluffers who make a show but have no real assets. "What is that? Bon Mahārāja's? Institute for Indian Culture and Philosophy, but where is your book?"

He was sharply critical of Tīrtha Mahārāja for using a picture of himself in his book with an effulgence around his head.

Gargamuni said that in all the temples Tīrtha manages, all the *ācāryas'* pictures are displayed, but only his picture has an effulgence.

Prabhupāda was quite disgusted. "Such a rascal. He has given Prabhupāda's picture no effulgence; his picture— effulgence. He's such a rascal. Publicly he's showing."

Jayapatāka humorously noted that his "effulgence" had to be painted on; he could not show it by natural means.

Prabhupāda shook his head. "Could not illuminate. Remain in darkness. Effulgence in darkness. And such a shameless man. He is giving effulgence in the picture."

Having discussed all their practical business in their previous meetings, their conversation this evening was lighter. Jayapatāka and Gargamuni both recounted stories of their recent preaching successes in Bengal.

Jayapatāka gave a pleasing summary of a program he recently held in Nadia district. "At one town, Beturhari, that, it is called Nakashiparathana. That's about thirty miles north of Māyāpur. One day in advance they advertised that we were coming and we were having a public showing of the cinema and Nitāi-Gaura *ārati*. And they had one *maidan* called Library Maidan. There was like one stage there. And when we came there and I saw the police in the afternoon, we told them we were going to have a function. So they said that 'We will send some policemen for keeping the order.' But that night so many people came; the space could only hold 4,000, but another 2-3,000 people came, and they were turned away because of insufficient space. So they were standing on the wall and on the rooftops all around, and all you could see were people's heads, just like an ocean.

"I chanted, 'Everyone please chant Hare Kṛṣṇa.' And I chanted the full *mantra* three times. They chanted so loud that even two, three blocks away people thought that the heavens were shouting. It was like a thunderbolt. And the policemen said that never—even the chief minister came here once, not even half so many people came, and that was announced for one week. This was announced for one day and more people came than ever before—he said, 'This really shows me that the people are hungry for spiritual answer.' They have no one to lead them."

Especially pleasing to Prabhupāda was the news of the sales of his Bengali language book, *Gītār-gāna*. The *sannyāsīs* said that everywhere they went people were asking for it, and some devotees were selling up to 200 at a time. It was becoming so popular that when Jayapatāka went to the Writer's Building in Calcutta on business about the land acquisition, workers there approached him to buy copies.

Jayapatāka said that the only difficulty was that we lacked Prabhupāda's books in local languages. To rectify this he has set up a team to begin translating the English books.
