We hope that you will be pleased by our efforts and we pray that we will increase our desire to please you more and more."

Prabhupāda was indeed happy to hear of his disciples' preaching efforts. "I thank you very much for the good news. The enthusiasm of the devotees is a very good sign. The more they become enthused and anxious to preach the more they become Krishna conscious; ya idam paramam guhyam mad-bhaktesv abhidhasyati, na ca tasman manusyesu kascin me priya-krttamah. One who explains the supreme secret to the devotees is the most dear to Krsna and never will there be one more dear. So always keep them enthused in this book distribution. This pleases me very much."

\* \* \*

Gurukṛpa Swami has arrived from Japan. He came in to see Śrīla Prabhupāda this morning to make his report. As he sat before His Divine Grace with Harikeśa to his right, he began telling Prabhupāda that his zone was too big. He said he could not visit Hawaii or Australia very much because of the distances and the expense involved. He also said he didn't like to go to Hawaii because he doesn't get along with Śukadeva prabhu and they simply fight whenever he goes.

Śrīla Prabhupāda was sitting back quietly listening as Gurukṛpa elaborated on the problems in Hawaii. Then, suddenly, he indicated Harikeśa Mahārāja with an upward tip of his head and said, "He can go."

It was completely unexpected. Surprised, I glanced at Harikeśa, who looked a little stunned and unsure whether what he had just heard was a serious comment or not.

But as Gurukṛpa continued speaking about his problems in Hawaii, Prabhupāda said it a second time: "So, he can go there."

Then we realized he was serious.

Prabhupāda began to complain that he wanted a GBC man to do his secretarial work. Indicating Harikeśa he said, "He is writing letters without my knowledge or approval. Actually no letter should go out unless it is seen by me."

Gurukṛpa also complained to Prabhupāda that Harikeśa has told Prabhupāda that he has been missing for the last week or two. The fact was, he said, that he has been traveling to places where we have no temple and was not "missing," but simply out of contact.

Prabhupāda said that Harikeśa was acting independently. Therefore he could not trust him to be his secretary any more. He said that there are three GBCs present in India, so one of them should become his secretary. He told Harikeśa, "Now you immediately go to Hawaii and take over as temple president there."

Harikeśa was dumbfounded. Although it has been obvious for the last few weeks that Śrīla Prabhupāda has been concerned about his engagement, there has not been even the slightest hint that Prabhupāda was thinking to change him.

Harikeśa looked flattened. Glumly he asked, "Well, what about the Eastern European program?"

"All right, you can go there if you want," Prabhupāda calmly said.

It appeared to me that Prabhupāda was using the problems in Hawaii as an opportunity to re-engage Harikeśa, and that the problem in Hawaii was not as important as the problem with Harikeśa.

Harikeśa, somewhat resistive to embracing Prabhupāda's sudden decision, presented various reasons why his work as secretary was apparently faulty. He went over the history of his previous service as temple president here in Vṛndāvana, and he offered various types of rationale for other objections raised. It seemed that he was trying to counter Prabhupāda's complaints; for every point that Prabhupāda raised, he had an excuse. This went on until finally Prabhupāda stopped him, and told him quite sternly, "It is not good to defend yourself so strongly in front of the spiritual master."

Lecturing him at length like a kind father, Prabhupāda told him that he should not think that he was rejecting him. He said, "I am not rejecting, I am engaging you properly. If management is not good, then we can change, but that does not mean that the man is being rejected. The spiritual master is equal to all. You are a good preacher and this Eastern European program is very important. I am very pleased with it. So you can go there and continue that work."

Dejectedly, Harikeśa returned to his room. A little later, when it sunk in that Prabhupāda did not want him as his secretary any more, but unable to understand how to cope with it, he went back to Śrīla Prabhupāda and announced, "Śrīla Prabhupāda, I quit!"

Prabhupāda looked at him as only a father can look a son who has just said something completely foolish, and in a very business-like way, said, "You can't quit, I fire you."

"As you like," Harikeśa responded gloomily.

"So what will you do?" Prabhupāda asked him.

"I guess I shall go back to Germany," Harikeśa replied.

Prabhupāda nodded and told him, "You should just go to the Schloss and sit there."

Harikeśa was unsure. "But Prabhupāda, there are so many troubles there, I don't know if I will be able to stay there."

But Prabhupāda was certain. He said, "You should just sit there, no matter what happens. You may do nothing else but chant Hare Kṛṣṇa, but just sit there and don't leave."

So Harikeśa finally agreed, "All right."

"And I will give you a loan of $900 for your ticket," Prabhupāda told him.

Harikeśa shook his head. "Śrīla Prabhupāda, I don't want your money."

"You must take it," Prabhupāda told him. "You must take this $900 and pay me back 10% interest."

"But I don't need your money," Harikeśa Mahārāja mildly protested.

"You *must* take it," Prabhupāda told him forcefully, repeating the order. "You must take this money and pay me back 10% interest."

Harikeśa Swami conceded. In a miserable mood he went off to pack his belongings.

\* \* \*

In the evening, Śrīla Prabhupāda, Hansadūta Swami and I sat in the back garden. Hansadūta suggested that if Harikeśa Mahārāja were to travel overland to Europe, he could visit the devotees who have recently set out to open centers in Kabul and Turkey. Thus he could enliven the devotees and also save $200 on his travel expenses. Śrīla Prabhupāda thought it a good idea and so he sent me up into the guest house to get Harikeśa.

When I entered his room, Harikeśa was sitting on the side of his bed, his suitcase half-packed, staring into space. I have rarely seen anyone so depressed. I told him that Śrīla Prabhupāda wanted to see him and so he came down into the garden. He offered his obeisances, still with a long face, and knelt before Śrīla Prabhupāda.

Prabhupāda looked at him brightly. "He says that if you go overland you can go for $100."

Harikeśa did not appreciate Hansadūta's suggestion, because he had made it without first asking what Harikeśa wanted to do. So, irritated, frustrated and dejected, he shot back sarcastically, "Well if I walk it will be even cheaper. I can go for $15."

Prabhupāda didn't like his attitude at all and he rebuked him sharply, "You simply create arguments! Here is some advice to help you, but instead of politely replying, you have to give some argument against it. This is your mentality. This is not at all good." With that, Prabhupāda let the matter drop and Harikeśa left the garden to complete his preparations to leave.

\* \* \*

The management continues to tax Prabhupāda's brain. With Harikeśa's removal, Prabhupāda initially decided to have Akṣayānanda Mahārāja as his secretary and install Hansadūta as the Vṛndāvana temple president. And so he had a long meeting with Hansadūta in the garden where he told him, "I will be very pleased if you can manage here nicely. The management is very, very bad. If you can simply make this guest house successful I will be very pleased. Other things are going on, but this guest house, this must be made successful." Prabhupāda is disturbed that no one is coming to stay in the guest house. He calculated that if he had invested the building costs of twenty five *lakhs* of rupees in fixed deposits then he would be realizing at least Rs. 20,000 a month in interest; but the guest house is only making about 4,000 a month. So there is an actual loss of 16,000 rupees a month.

Prabhupāda was also frank about Hansadūta's reputation as a manager. He told him, "Previously there was some complaint, but if you make this place a success then,"—he held his hand out as if turning a key—"all mouths will be closed up tight." He made a comparison with how so many people, especially his Godbrothers, have complained about the way he has spread Kṛṣṇa consciousness, but because of his success, "No one is allowed to speak anything. All mouths locked tight shut!" He gave Hansadūta all encouragement to make Vṛndāvana a success; otherwise he is becoming hopeless that it will ever be managed nicely.

But then a little while later he changed his mind, deciding to have Hansadūta serve as his secretary.

In the late evening, as he sat in his *prasādam* room drinking hot milk, Prabhupāda asked me if I thought Akṣayānanda could manage.

I spoke honestly. "No, Śrīla Prabhupāda. He simply agrees with everything you say, but nothing is changed."

Prabhupāda laughed and mimicked Akṣayānanda's standard response to Prabhupāda's many complaints. "'Yes Prabhupāda, that's right Prabhupāda. You are correct!.'" Shaking his head in good-natured resignation, he added, "Still he is devotee. He may not be expert, but he is a devotee and that is his qualification."

So Prabhupāda decided to revert back to his original decision and appoint Akṣayānanda as his new secretary. He said that he will even teach him Hindi if he wants to learn.

## September 23rd, 1976

In the early morning Śrīla Prabhupāda called in Akṣayānanda Swami to inform him of his appointment as secretary.

Akṣayānanda nodded dutifully, "Whatever you think best Prabhupāda." It was obvious that he is attached to his service as temple president and that he is doubtful about Hansadūta managing well. Nevertheless he is happy to serve Prabhupāda in whatever capacity His Divine Grace requests.

Harikeśa Mahārāja came in for a few moments and took a last *darśana* of Śrīla Prabhupāda. With His Divine Grace's full blessing, he left for Delhi at 6 a.m.

\* \* \*

During class Śrīla Prabhupāda made an interesting observation about the *brahmāstra* weapon as he pointed out that modern scientists have no information about the subtle aspects of nature. "So they have no knowledge. Therefore they can manufacture weapon or bomb with the gross things. *Bhūmir āpo 'nalo*—the chemicals, that is gross. But this *brahmāstra* is not gross; this is also material, but it is made of subtle things—mind, intelligence and ego. Therefore Arjuna is asking Kṛṣṇa, 'I do not know wherefrom this such high temperature is coming.'"

Prabhupāda gave several examples of the subtle movements of the soul, and concluded that if we want to know anything we have to follow Arjuna's example and approach Kṛṣṇa, for only He can reveal the true nature of things. "These laws they do not know, how things are happening in the subtle ways. Arjuna knows, but for our education he's asking Kṛṣṇa that 'Wherefrom this high temperature is coming?' So many things are there, even in this material world we cannot understand, we cannot get full information. But if we take Kṛṣṇa's instruction ... He's giving personally the instruction in the *Bhagavad-gītā*. If we take care of them, then we can understand everything very easily. Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement is so nice that simply by understanding Kṛṣṇa, you can understand everything. So this is the all-perfect knowledge, perfect culture, perfect advancement of civilization. Everyone should take to it and all questions are answered by Kṛṣṇa. You take it and become a perfect man."

\* \* \*

Akṣayānanda Mahārāja took up his duties right away. He brought the day's mail in to Śrīla Prabhupāda in mid-morning. There was a letter from Girirāja prabhu dated the 18th and addressed to Harikeśa Swami. Akṣayānanda read it out to Prabhupāda. In it Girirāja said that the editor of *Bhavan's Journal* wants to publish Prabhupāda's reply to their questionnaire and so needs the answers immediately.

On another topic Girirāja wrote, "Meanwhile one of the devotees approached a very important Vaisnava of Bombay and that Vaisnava was troubled by the incident about Ballabhacharya quoted in Back to Godhead. He has pledged his full support to ISKCON if we can clear this misunderstanding. Therefore we have to request you to immediately send a copy of Srila Prabhupada's reply to Smt. Morarjee so that we can adapt it and write a letter to this gentleman."

He added that Bombay was progressing nicely and Gopāla Kṛṣṇa prabhu would give a full report when he arrives in Vṛndāvana next week.

Śrīla Prabhupāda sent him a short reply, informing him that the *Bhavan's Journal* article has already been sent and that Harikeśa Mahārāja has sent out the copy of Sumati Morarjee's letter. He added, "Harikesa is not working as my secretary now; he has been sent for preaching work."

Rūpānuga prabhu sent a comprehensive report of his GBC zone, which includes Ottawa, Montreal, Philadelphia, Baltimore, Washington D. C., and St. Louis and its satellite farm. Before detailing the temples' activities, he gave an update on the Bhaktivedanta Institute. He said that work was progressing on the book they were planning and some of the material would be used in the first issue of the BI's journal, *Sa-vijñanam*, which he expected to come out by the end of November. He proposed that initially the journal would appear twice a year, and then quarterly. He plans to set up a headquarters for the BI in the New England/Boston area, "the educational capital of America."

Rūpānuga said that Svarūpa Dāmodara prabhu was going for his final interview for residency in America on September 13. He expected to receive approval within three weeks. Then, when his obligation to Emery University expires in December, Svarūpa Dāmodara would come to India to see Prabhupāda and arrange for him to go to Manipur.

About himself, Rūpānuga said that he has teamed up with Arjuna Mullik, a psychologist from the University of Madras, who met Śrīla Prabhupāda in July in New York. Rūpānuga is also writing, and in this context he had a complaint. "I am working on one article for the Journal entitled, 'A Morphology of Consciousness.' In this connection, we feel that the editorial policy of BTG is narrow-minded regarding scientific articles. Damodar prabhu (an editor on the BTG staff) and Jayadvaita das also agree with this opinion. A case in point is that the article recently published by the scientists in BTG was originally rejected and was later printed only because Your Divine Grace requested it. Other articles from Rabindra Swarup have been rejected and more recently one by myself and another by Amarendra das, president of Gainesville, who is one of our best preachers and a graduate in journalism. The policy, according to Damodar, is for BTG to publish articles of general interest, rather than those of 'specific interest' like more scientific or scholarly articles. In my opinion, there could be a scientific-type article from different fields in every issue of BTG because many readers of BTG are intelligent. Of course the most scientific or scholarly articles or more technical articles can be for the journal, but others who are qualified should have a chance to publish in BTG. I know, for example, that Amarendra worked on his article for months and received a letter in reply that he should read a book on writing style. Anyway, I am bringing this to your attention because it has become a familiar observation by the more senior members of our Society."

The rest of his letter comprised his summary report on the individual temples. St. Louis was the top small temple for book distribution and Philadelphia the top medium temple. In Washington, Gabhīra dāsa, our Chaplain at the University of Maryland, has started a cooking class which attracted sixty students at the first meeting and he had an article published in the University paper which has a circulation of 35,000. Each temple report was upbeat. Only about Baltimore did Rūpānuga report a decrease as well as some difficulties executing a plan to purchase some property for a farm. The devotees are currently using a property owned by the father of Aghāri dāsa. Rūpānuga said that he had decided to disband the project and send the twelve cows and six devotees to other farm projects, especially St. Louis. He felt this would also free up more time for himself so that he can concentrate on the development of the BI.

He added that he had recently undertaken a tour with Tamal Krishna and Tripurāri Mahārājas to St. Louis, Philadelphia and Washington D.C. and the result was an average increase in collections of between $5,000-$10,000 per month. "The results of this team work have been very encouraging," he wrote. "As far as Tamal Krishna is concerned, I am happy to report that he is showing a new cooperative attitude that in fact is increasing book distribution like never before, and has been demonstrated by our recent working together. ... In this way, if the GBC men, with their various talents, portfolios etc., can work together, Your Divine Grace will be assured that the management of ISKCON is going on and concentrate on the books."

Rūpānuga enclosed a check for $1,000 which, he said, "I hope will help to mitigate any headaches caused by this letter."

Prabhupāda heard the report with interest. He was concerned about Rūpānuga's dissatisfaction with BTG, especially in view of the recent complaint by Sumati Morarjee. He wrote back, "Regarding the editorial policy of BTG, if the editorial board is not expert enough they should be changed. Dr. O.B.L. Kapoor also had put a similar complaint. Yes, scientific articles must be published when sent by our men. I cannot see every article, but some of you should examine why nice articles are rejected. See if the board can be changed. If experienced editors are not there it will be unpopular magazine. These things are to be seen to immediately by the GBC. The board should be judged immediately and be changed if required."

As far as the Baltimore farm is concerned, Prabhupāda told him not to worry. "Don't increase the field of activity if there is not sufficient money. There is no need of farm project there at Baltimore if the money is deficient. The Bhaktivedanta Institute must be very sound regarding income, otherwise how it will run on."

\* \* \*

In the evening Śrīla Prabhupāda met once more with Hansadūta Mahārāja, discussing his plans to revamp the temple management. Prabhupāda is giving him a lot of time and encouragement with the hope that he can improve things.

\* \* \*

I asked Gurukṛpa Swami whether there was any substance to the rumor that Madhudviṣa took money from Australia. He shrugged and said that nothing can be proved and, since he has already left, it doesn't matter much. From what he told me about the Australian *yātrā*, it seems that things are not going too well. There have been several marriages, there are no new devotees joining, one of the top book distributors has blooped, and another leading manager "is on the way out."

## September 24th, 1976

Śrīla Prabhupāda summoned me into his room on the roof with a ring of his bell at 1:50 a.m. this morning. I went in, offered my obeisances, and when I looked up, Śrīla Prabhupāda told me to sit down. Then he asked me for my opinion on the new arrangements he has made for the Vṛndāvana management. "Confidentially, what is your opinion of Harikeśa?"

I was surprised that he sought my opinion; how could *my* view of anything be of any possible use to Prabhupāda? How could I give advice to my spiritual master?

Seeing my hesitancy, Prabhupāda reassured me. "No, after all, you have an English brain, and they are good at observing situations. So just consider what can be done here to improve things."

With this encouragement I tried to respond as best I could. He asked whether I thought Harikeśa might be good as the temple president in Vṛndāvana, because previously he had held that position for a few months. I answered that I thought Harikeśa would be better situated in the Eastern European program, and I gave two reasons: for his own sake he needs a bigger scale service—his brain is so active he might cause a disturbance in small project like Vṛndāvana. And in addition, the Eastern European program was virtually dependent on his personal presence.

Then Prabhupāda asked me what I thought about Akṣayānanda. I told him that he seemed ideal as Prabhupāda's secretary. He has the right mentality for this type of service, and in India Śrīla Prabhupāda often needs the assistance of someone who can speak Hindi, both for reading and replying to Hindi letters, as well as for receiving guests. Moreover, Akṣayānanda knows how to deal nicely with Indian gentlemen.

Finally he asked me about Hansadūta. But he was mostly an unknown quantity to me. "Well, he says he can do something and he is enthusiastic to try. So I would give him a chance, and see how he does."

Prabhupāda listened carefully to what I had to say. He then thanked me and sent me back to rest.

I feel honored that Prabhupāda would even consider asking for my opinion. His comment about my having an "English brain" was a revealing insight into his intelligence in seeing how every living entity is offered a particular facility by the laws of nature—a particular birth in a particular place means one gets certain propensities. The English have a good reputation for managerial skills, especially here in India, where they were able to manage 400 million people with just a few thousand men. It seems Prabhupāda therefore considered that since I have an English brain, I should be able use it for managerial purposes.

\* \* \*

Several times over the last few weeks Prabhupāda has been disturbed by the poor quality of flowers on the Deity garlands. Sometimes also, the Deities do not even have garlands on when the curtains are opened for Their morning *darśana*. When Prabhupāda greeted Them this morning, he saw that Śrī Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Balarāma yet again had no garlands. Openly aggravated, he half-turned to Akṣayānanda and told him sternly, "This is another farce!"

He was so troubled by the poor standard of worship, that he dedicated most of his class to it. Although his tone was dispassionate and objective, showing no traces of the flash of anger he had displayed earlier, he gave a very strong warning to the devotees about the consequences of inattention and neglect.

He started out by saying that human life begins with the practice of religion, but nowadays there are organized movements such as communism to stop it. Yet, he said, in one way, they cannot be blamed. "Because the guardians of the religious system, they are fallen. Just like immediately our Śubhavilāsa prabhu was asking me that, 'We have seen so many temples. Why they are so neglected?' Is it not your question? And why they should not neglect it? Mostly, the temples, they have become the means of livelihood. That is the defect. Temple is not meant for means of livelihood; then it will deteriorate. How long you can falsely worship Deity and make show of *ārati*? You cannot go on very long time, that is not possible. You'll be disgusted. Unless there is feeling, *bhāva*, that 'Here is Kṛṣṇa. Kṛṣṇa has very kindly come here to receive, to take, accept my humble service. He's so great that He cannot be approached by a person like me.' *Aṇor aṇīyān mahato mahīyān*."

Explaining that we cannot worship Kṛṣṇa in His universal aspect Prabhupāda went on, "Therefore He is so kind that He has appeared before you in this temple so that you can touch Him actually, you can serve Him, you can dress Him, you can offer Him eatables ... This is *arcā-vigraha*, Deity. *Arcye viṣṇau śilā-dhīḥ*. Kṛṣṇa has appeared.

"We are not so elevated like Nanda Mahārāja or Yaśodā," he said. "We're just beginners. So we do not know what is Kṛṣṇa. We cannot see Kṛṣṇa, either His *virāḍ-mūrti* or this *mūrti*. So what we can see? We can see stone, wood or material things. So when Kṛṣṇa appears to be seen by you and He appears like a stone statue, He's not stone statue. Don't think. Therefore we must learn how to see Kṛṣṇa. So we should not think that 'Here is a stone statue.' As soon as we think of stone statue, then our, this feeling, *bhāva*, will be lost. So the answer is that if we establish some temple and Deity and take it as a means of livelihood ..."

"So at least we Indians we are trained up like that. Not only trained up, we are born devotees. Anyone who has taken birth in India, that is special facility. In their previous birth, they had performed many austerities, much austerities. Even the demigods, they desire also to take birth in India to get this opportunity. So India-India means this planet, Bhāratavarṣa—there is good opportunity. So if we think that 'Here is a stone statue,' then it will not prolong many days.

"*Galagraha*. No more *vigraha*, but *galagraha*. Suppose I have established this temple. Now under my direction, my disciples are worshiping *vigraha*. *Vigraha* means the form of the Lord, *rūpa*. But if there is no following of the regulative principles, then after my death it will be *galagraha*, a burden, that 'Our rascal Guru Mahārāja established this temple, and we have to worship, early rise in the morning, all botheration.' That is called *galagraha*, a burden, 'He has left with us a burden.' This is the risk. Then such a big temple will be mismanaged, and you'll find that 'This is breaking' and 'This is unclean,' and there is no attention. This will be our \[mood\] ... That is called *galagraha*, 'The rascal has given us a burden.

"So it is very difficult. If we have lost that feeling that 'Here is Kṛṣṇa. Here is a chance to serve Him ...' *Śrī-vigrahārādhana-nitya-nānā-śṛṅgāra-tan-mandira-mārjanādau*. Therefore we are very much vigilant, 'Why you did not this? Why you do not this? Why ...?' As soon as the feeling of devotional service will be lost, this temple will be a burden. This is the way. It will be such a big temple, to manage, it will be a great burden. So they are feeling burden. Therefore they don't mind if somewhere is broken sometimes. 'All right, whatever money we have got, let us eat first of all.' This is the position. *Vigraha* and *galagraha*, you should understand. If we forget that 'Here is Kṛṣṇa personally present. We have to receive Him very nicely. We have to give Him nice food, nice dress ...' Then it is service. And as soon as the feeling comes that 'Here is a stone idol,'—they say sometimes 'idol worship'—'and we have been instructed to dress Him, to give Him ...—all botheration.' Then finished. Finished.

"That has come everywhere. I have seen in Nasik in many, many big temples there is no *pūjārī*, and the dogs are passing stool."

Prabhupāda said that this same problem was also present in the West. Churches were derelict and he had personally observed that on Sundays only the caretaker and few old women were attending. Many of these disused churches were up for sale but even then the priests have been reluctant to sell to us. "One church, the priest said that 'I shall set fire in this church, still I shall not give to Bhaktivedanta Swami.'" Prabhupāda grinned and, as everyone laughed, he went on, "This Toronto church was like that also. And in Melbourne the sale condition was that 'You have to dismantle this church building.' We said, 'Why?' He said, '\[If you\] Utilize as temple now, then we shall not give you.' They refused. So they do not like that 'This Kṛṣṇa consciousness movement will purchase our churches and install Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa Deity.' They do not like that."

Despite his injection of a little humor Prabhupāda remained very serious about the problems he detected here, exemplified by the failure of the *pūjārīs* to offer nice garlands to the Deities. He analyzed the mentality behind it and spelled out the consequences in strikingly frank terms.

"So not only the churches in the Western countries, here also. As soon as you will lose the spirit of service, this temple will become a big *go-down* \[warehouse\], that's all. No more temple. So we have to maintain that service spirit. Therefore we are so much particular—'Why fresh flower is not there?' If you think, 'Here is a stone statue. What is the meaning of fresh flower or old flower? We have to give some flower, that's all.' But no feeling, that 'Here is Kṛṣṇa. We must give fresh flower.' Just like I'm a living man, if you give me a fresh flower, and if you bring some garbage, and if you give me, shall I be pleased? Do you think? So this feeling is losing even in the beginning, that 'We shall satisfy this statue with some rubbish, garbage flowers. He's not going to protest.' Yes, He'll not protest, but your life will be finished. The protest will come like that. As soon as you lost the feeling, *bhāva*, *budhā bhāva-samanvitāḥ*.

"Who can worship Kṛṣṇa? When there is *bhāva*, *sthāyi-bhāva*. This has been discussed in *Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu*, what is *bhāva*. But if you have no *bhāva*, then you are on the material, *kaniṣṭha-adhikārī*. Simply show. A show cannot go on many days, show will be finished very soon."

\* \* \*

Prabhupāda sent a letter today to Jayatīrtha prabhu, the GBC of England and Germany, informing him of Harikeśa Swami's imminent arrival. "Harikesa was doing nice preaching work and recently he has received one letter from Sucandra. Both of them can work there very nicely. So, as you know, I am interested very much for preaching work. I have sent him yesterday to Poland etc. I have given him one month's expenditure, also including his fare. I have paid him $950.00. He's enthusiastic to preach in that part of the world in co-operation with Sucandra. Try to encourage him in preaching work. So far this $950.00 it is given to him as loan and is to be returned as soon as possible."

There was also another letter from Gurudāsa Mahārāja, informing Śrīla Prabhupāda that since his last letter he has recovered his *daṇḍa*. He sent a heavy letter to the airport authorities in Poland, claiming $300 damages and threatening "diplomatic implications." The result was that within hours they found the *daṇḍa* and sent it to Stockholm. Gurudāsa also reported that his party is doing nicely and they are purchasing a van for their overland trip to India at the end of the year. Jayatīrtha has also arranged for him to do a college preaching tour in England.

Śrīla Prabhupāda replied along the same lines as his last letter to Gurudāsa. "Harikesa has gone there to Poland to preach as you are doing, so take him with you. I have given him $1,000.00 for immediate expenditure and he has to return this as soon as possible. So he has gone yesterday morning, perhaps by this time he has reached. He likes to work jointly with Sucandra, but if Sucandra is not free then he may join with you."

Lokanātha Mahārāja sent in his first report of the progress of his bullockcart traveling SKP. It was sent from the Goverdhan Hotel, Delhi Gate, Agra, and dated September 21st. He said that so far they have visited five villages, where they held *kīrtana* through the streets in both the morning and evening, and then a program with chanting, *ārati*, an explanation of Śrīla Prabhupāda's mission and *prasādam* distribution in the evenings. During the morning sessions they would collect various ingredients such as flour, *dāl*, vegetables, milk and sugarcane *gur* and cook this into *halva* and *khichari*. After offering it to Gaura-Nitāi, they distributed the *prasādam*at the evening program. At their last venue over four hundred people attended the program "and all were satisfied."

"After being on the road for some time now we are realizing a need of having our own bullock cart," Lokanātha wrote. "So we will be in Agra for 3-4 days to try to raise some funds to get a bullock cart. Then our program will be more regular and together. I am happy with this engagement. Program is very simple but very potent and purifying one."

Prabhupāda smiled brightly hearing the news. He wrote back, "I am also happy to hear your very nice activities. I wish I could have joined you. I like your program very much. If you continue this program you will be benefited, people will be benefited, and everyone will be happy.

"If possible you can collect something for our Gurukula and Temple also, and if some high-class men want to offer their children to Gurukula we can accept."

Yaśomatīnandana prabhu sent a package from Gujarat. His preaching report was upbeat: on Rādhāṣṭamī they moved into new temple premises at 7 Kailash Society, Ashram Rd. Navrangpura, Ahmedabad. About 75% of his life members attended the successful opening and they served *prasādam* to over 500 people. Because they had held a press conference the day before, all the newspapers reported on the event very favorably. He is now looking for some land because he has about Rs. 65,000 in the bank.

He enclosed a copy of a new Gujarati magazine he has published, which came off the press on Janmāṣṭamī, and he has translated *The Scientific Basis of Krishna Consciousness*, and is working now on *Easy Journey to Other Planets*. He asked Prabhupāda's permission to publish these two books as one volume, since they both deal with science.

Another enclosure he included was an article printed in a Gujarati language weekly magazine with a circulation of 50,000. Yaśomatīnandana went to the trouble of translating and typing it out. It was similar in tone to the *Blitz*. It described Śrīla Prabhupāda's activities in spreading Kṛṣṇa consciousness as a "booming import-export business," exporting religion and importing foreigners and foreign money. It questioned the source of our income: "The Government is worried that the devotees of Krishna may be secretly eating the installments of CIA just as Lord Krishna Himself used to secretly steal the butter and eat it."

Although the article said that our main center is in W. Bengal it also stated, "West Bengal is factually the birth place of Swamiji, but he is not taking any interest in their Calcutta and Mayapur ashrams. These two ashrams are run by one American boy, Gregory Scharf. Scharf has changed his name and now it is Gargamuni Swami and he wears saffron robes. Sometime ago he said that 'We have expanded more than the British Empire.' This expansion is due to money and from where this society gets its money that nobody knows, the government only knows that all the money is coming from the U.S.A. and every year it is increasing." It quoted Gargamuni as saying that all our money comes from the sale of Spiritual Sky products, and the writer doubted that an incense and cosmetic products company could realize the kind of money that ISKCON is spending in India.

Yaśomatīnandana conjectured that this and the *Blitz* articles are being disseminated by the same party. He asked Prabhupāda if he should pursue legal action against the magazine, adding that a good lawyer had advised him that we have a sound case for defamation, but that it would be a protracted procedure and we may not gain anything.

Prabhupāda was glad to hear about the new center, and urged him to purchase some land as soon as possible. He was also happy about our new publication. As far as the adverse publicity is concerned, he told him, "Regarding against propaganda, it is going on practically everywhere, especially Bengal. So we have to work very sincerely and Krishna will give us protection. The only hope, we can understand that demons are disturbed. That is quite natural. When Krishna was born, from the day of His birth, the demons wanted to kill him in so many ways but practically it was found that demons were killed by Krishna and He established His mission yada yada hi dharmasya glanir bhavati bharata/ abhyutthanam adharmasya tadatmanam srjamyaham. So if we work sincerely, the Krishna Consciousness Movement is non-different from Krishna. As Krishna killed all the demons, we should also be able to kill all demons if we remain faithful in the discharge of our mission."

Śukadeva prabhu sent a short letter from Hawaii. He inquired what to do about their Pañca-tattva Deities, which are made of papier-mâchī. He said the bottom of the Deities stands are now looking very ragged. Although they have plans to build a new temple and install new Deities, that will not happen for some time. He wondered whether they should attempt to repair the existing Deities or leave Them. He asked, "What are the guidelines to know whether we should repair the Deities so that it is not done on our whim. I have not heard of any standard throughout our Society."

Śrīla Prabhupāda declined to involve himself, and told Śukadeva that Gurukṛpa Swami, who left here this morning, was on his way there. He said that whatever he advised, should be done.

\* \* \*

A devotee reported that Harikeśa Swami is still in Delhi. As soon as he arrived there he became very ill and is unable to travel.

Also Gopāla Kṛṣṇa prabhu was supposed to be in Delhi but hasn't been seen. Prabhupāda is concerned.

## September 25th, 1976

A devotee arrived from Los Angeles in the early morning, bringing Śrīla Prabhupāda two gilt-edged copies of the new *Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam* Eighth Canto Part One. Śrīla Prabhupāda received them with great pleasure, happy that the BBT is now keeping pace with his translation work.

\* \* \*

In class Śrīla Prabhupāda made some interesting points about the spiritual origins of violence. The verses described how Arjuna prepared to fire his own *brahmāstra* to counteract the one thrown by Aśvatthāmā, and Prabhupāda explained that knowledge of warfare is one of the sections of the *Vedas*. "*Dhanur Veda*, how to utilize *dhanuḥ*. *Dhanuḥ* means bow and arrows. Similarly *Āyur Veda*. *Āyur Veda* means medical science, how to protect the *āyuḥ*. Because the body is perishable, so in the Vedic knowledge, everything is there to guide the human society."

He compared the *Vedas* to the desire trees of the spiritual world, which can supply anything on demand. "*Vedas* you can have all different types of knowledge: namely material knowledge and spiritual knowledge, both, perfectly. Because we have now forgotten our spiritual energy, we do not cultivate spiritual energy; therefore the *Veda* is there."

Thus knowledge of warfare is included in the *Vedas*. "So the killing art is there. You cannot make it null and void by advocating nonviolence, no. That is required. Violence is also a part of the society. Just like here is some itching sensation; this is violence. That is required for the comfort. So similarly, Arjuna was *kṣatriya*. He knew the art of killing. And Kṛṣṇa also, He appeared as a *kṣatriya* in the dynasty of *kṣatriyas*; Vāsudeva, son of Vasudeva. He also knew the art of killing. That is also one of the part of His business. *Yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati bhārata, paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṁ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām*. So *vināśa—*requires violence. So we cannot decry violence. Kṛṣṇa was speaking *Bhagavad-gītā*, the science of God, in the battlefield of Kurukṣetra. We cannot condemn violence, that is not possible. But there is no violence in the spiritual world, that is a fact. Violence is only in the material world."

Prabhupāda explained that because all desires are coming from Kṛṣṇa, everything we have experience of is there in God. "Therefore He's God. Not that minus something. Nothing minus. Everything. *Akhila-rasāmṛta-sindhu; raso vai saḥ*; He is the reservoir of all *rasa*, humor or mellow. So this is also a mellow. Sometimes cruel men, they take pleasure by killing. I've seen it. One hotel man was cutting the throat of one chicken, half-cut, and it was throbbing, jumping. His child was crying because he could not see such horrible thing. And the hotel man, he was laughing and pacifying the child, 'Why you are crying? Just see how he's throbbing, how he's jumping.' So one subject matter, the *rasa* is different, humor is different. He's enjoying one *rasa*, the father, and the child is crying; that is also another *rasa*. So the whole world is full of *rasa*.

"The sex life is called *ādi-rasa*. *Ādi-rasa* means conjugal love. This whole world is existing on *mithunī-bhāva*, sex. So wherefrom it comes, this *ādi-rasa*? Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura has described in his comment on *Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam*, in the beginning, that Kṛṣṇa is the origin of *ādi-rasa-janmādy asya*. From there, this *ādi-rasa* is generated. That is Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa. So everything is there. Otherwise, imperfectness. So as there is *ādi-rasa*, Kṛṣṇa is enjoying with the *gopīs* and Rādhārāṇī, similarly, He enjoys with *bībhatsa-rasa, vīra-rasa*, killing. Killing is also *vīra-rasa*. Because He is the reservoir of all *rasas*. So do not think that this violence or fighting is bad, no. Nothing is bad when it is utilized for Kṛṣṇa. And nothing is good when it is utilized for your sense gratification."

\* \* \*

Prabhupāda is very concerned about Gopāla Kṛṣṇa prabhu. He was supposed to be in Delhi two or three days ago but hasn't shown up. No one seems to know where he is. Prabhupāda is aware that Gopāla is disturbed by conflicts with Hansadūta and other leaders here in India, and thinks he may have left India. During his massage he said that he thinks Gopāla is a little attracted to his family and may have gone to join them. So Prabhupāda sent a telegram to Bombay reading simply, "Where is Gopal Krishna?"

A letter came from Bhaktijan dāsa, one of Prabhupāda's early disciples from New York. Bhaktijan has a reputation for eccentricity. He wrote in a rather complaining tone that not much effort was being made by the temples to preach to the black population in America \[he is white\] and suggested that something be done to rectify this. He also inquired about taking *sannyāsa*, ending his letter with an expression of concern over reports of Śrīla Prabhupāda's ill health. He said he feared for Prabhupāda's departure.

Prabhupāda had a positive remedy for the apparent neglect Bhaktijan had pointed out: "Why not make preaching with black people in America your lifetime preaching goal? Yes, limit to this. You preach—that is sannyasa. What is the use of changing dress? Do, actually. Regarding my leaving, I'll not leave the planet until you order."

\* \* \*

Prabhupāda has not been receiving many visitors, but he continues to give his afternoon *darśanas* in the temple courtyard, and he is still meeting regularly with Prem Yogi, who seems to be making good progress in devotional life.

Prabhupāda is also conferring regularly with Hansadūta Mahārāja, who seems to have thrown himself with gusto into the temple management.

## September 26th, 1976

Hardly a day goes by without Śrīla Prabhupāda saying something about the deficiencies of modern science and its proponents, exposing their faulty logic and limited vision. *Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam* class is the perfect platform from which to do so. Speaking this morning on verses [1.7.30-31](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-1/7.30) he described the disturbance to the inhabitants of the different planetary systems caused by the combination of the two *brahmāstras* thrown by Aśvatthāma and Arjuna.

Prabhupāda took full advantage of that description to once more challenge the modern scientists. "Everywhere there is *prajā*, there is living entities. Otherwise, how it is said *trīl lokān*? It is a foolish theory that there is no life in other planets. A rascal theory, it has no meaning. We have got many evidences. I do not know why these rascal scientists say that there is no life in other planet. Why? The other planet is also made of the *pañca-bhūta*, *pṛthvī-ap-tejas-vāyu-ākāśa*. They are not different; maybe something is very prominent. Just like in the sun globe, the fire is prominent. Fire is also one of the five elements: *pṛthvī-ap-tejas*. That does not mean there is no life. There must be, otherwise, how Kṛṣṇa talked with the sun-god, *imaṁ vivasvate yogaṁ proktavān aham avyayam*? And the living entity, *nainaṁ dahati pāvakaḥ*, the living entity is not burned by the fire, it is not dried up, it is not moistened. This is stated. So why there will be no life in the sun globe? There must be. So there are germs in the fire also, *agni-pok*. So we are being misled by the so-called scientists; that is not perfect knowledge. The perfect knowledge is in the *Vedas*. Therefore it is advised, *tad-vijñānārthaṁ sa gurum evābhigacchet śrotriyaṁ brahma-niṣṭham*: you should go to a guru who has complete knowledge from the *śruti*. *Śruti* means *Vedas*. *Ācāryavān puruṣo veda*. *Veda* means you have to approach *ācārya*. He knows everything. Unless he is follower of the *Vedas*, *śruti*, he's a rascal. What is the use of going there?"

\* \* \*

Prabhupāda replied to three pieces of mail during his noon massage. All the letters were from Los Angeles. Rādhāballabha had sent an accompanying letter with the two volumes of the new Eighth Canto *Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam*. He informed Śrīla Prabhupāda that the new book was offered on the altar on September 17, the anniversary of Śrīla Prabhupāda's arrival in America, and said, "I am sure that in the future this day will be declared a National Holiday, a day in which all Americans will chant and hear about your glorious activities. You are the real national hero, not mlecchas like George Washington and Abraham Lincoln."

Rādhāballabha also mentioned that the new reprint of *Bhagavad-gītā* is complete.

Śrīla Prabhupāda send back a short reply thanking him for the books.

Another letter was from Kāraṇdhara prabhu, who said that he was feeling greatly inspired and determined after receiving Prabhupāda's letter to him at the end of last month. He has already begun collecting funds for the construction of a skyscraper on the vacant lot next to the temple. So far he has $3,000 and he expects to receive another $15,000-$30,000 in the next three or four months. "Of course, this amount is nothing compared to the 7 to 10 million that is required but I know that by Your Grace anything can be accomplished. I am prepared to expend this life and body for this project so long as it receives Your sanction. Your blessing is all I require to sustain enthusiasm." He informed Prabhupāda that next month they will begin work on a new *āśrama* building on Watseka Ave. opposite the temple, with facility for seventy residents.

Kāraṇdhara said that along with Īśāna and Raṇadhīra prabhus, he has been working to produce a new type of fiberglass *mṛdaṅga*. They expect to go fully into production by November and make about 2,500 drums a year. Kāraṇdhara ended his letter with a nice glorification of Śrīla Prabhupāda and a plea for his extra mercy.

Prabhupāda was happy to hear from him again. He replied with a short letter of encouragement. "Regarding the skyscraper scheme, yes, that I have already sanctioned since the idea was given to me by you.

"If you make 2500 mrdangas per year, that is very good, then distribute to the whole of American people."

The third letter was a thorough report from Rāmeśvara Swami on his recent trip to Fiji and Australia. He spent several days in Fiji with Deoji Punja, Vāsudeva prabhu. He was impressed with Vāsudeva's serious approach to Kṛṣṇa consciousness and observed that he was chanting thirty-two rounds per day, offering all his food, and personally working hard to raise the money for the temple construction. So far he has collected $74,000.

Rāmeśvara offered two main reasons why difficulty has arisen over the ownership of the land. He felt Upendra was not properly qualified to preach there. Upendra had disagreed with Vāsudeva on many minor things. In addition, Upendra was unable to do anything to support his family and so was financially dependant on Vāsudeva's personal funds. He was not inclined to make life members, although this was the main source of money for building the temple. Thus Upendra's and Vāsudeva's relationship became so strained that Upendra has now returned to America. Rāmeśvara added that Upendra's difficulty in dealing with the local men has exacerbated previous bad experiences they have had with other foreign devotees who have gone there to preach in the past.

This lead to the second major problem: the land was jointly owned by Vāsudeva and his brothers. One brother is a devotee but the others, who are not, were fearful that in the future there may be some mismanagement, or the land and temple might be sold against their will. This sense of fear was increased by Śrīla Prabhupāda's writing directly to the local bank manager, telling him not to give any loans out to ISKCON Fiji without his personal approval. That was why, although they did transfer the land out of their personal names, it was put into the ownership of "the trustees of ISKCON" but not ISKCON Fiji itself. The trustees, which include the brothers, are all local men. Rāmeśvara said that Vāsudeva himself has full faith in Prabhupāda and does not share his brothers mistrust, but he cannot overrule them.

Technically, Vāsudeva did not violate Prabhupāda's instruction to the bank manager, because the loan was taken out in the name of "the trustees of ISKCON" and not in the name of ISKCON Fiji. Thus the trustees are individually responsible for the loan's repayment. Rāmeśvara wrote, "The fact is that without the loan, the construction on the temple would have halted. That would have ruined our reputation and made further collecting towards the temple very difficult." He said that the temple would be one of the most impressive structures in Fiji. "Many times the local Hindus have tried to construct a decent temple, but have always failed. Now they see this magnificent temple and are greatly awed by Your Divine Grace and the ISKCON movement."

Rāmeśvara offered a solution to alleviate the brothers fears: "In the official constitution, Your Divine Grace has already been given absolute authority in all matters. The brothers will all be satisfied by amending the constitution to state that the new temple and land can never be sold, mortgaged, put up as security for loans, leased, etc. but remains permanent property of ISKCON Fiji. Then they will no longer fear that ISKCON may one day sell the temple. Once this is done, we can add Your Divine Grace and Tamal Krishna Maharaja (GBC Chairman) as permanent trustees, etc. No one will object.

"In fact Vasudeva is looking forwarded to having us send a good man to act as temple president, and he will simply help supply funds for repaying the loan by more life memberships. ... We can probably sell 2,000 BTGs per month, as well as collect donations at the temple itself, distribute prasadam profusely, organize big kirtans etc. In this way the temple overhead will be easily maintained and we can have great success."

Rāmeśvara felt that the only problem was that Vāsudeva was feeling that Śrīla Prabhupāda was displeased and had lost confidence in him. He stressed Vāsudeva's good intent. "At no time did I detect any insincerity in Vasudeva—he is simply under pressure from his brothers, but our solution should satisfy everyone; thus ISKCON Fiji can flourish."

Rāmeśvara added that he and Gurukṛpa Swami felt that once the temple is open, two book distributors and two *pūjārīs* could be sent from Australia. As well as this, he said a local scholar was now translating Prabhupāda's books and BTG into the Fijian language. His work would be checked by Vāsudeva, and Rāmeśvara volunteered to publish it.

Rāmeśvara concluded, "Vasudeva is very desirous of always remaining in association of ISKCON devotees and simply hopes that they will behave better and steadier than the ones previously in Fiji. The selection of the president is very important in this regards. I feel confident that the problems are now resolved and immediately following Gaura Purnima 1977 we will have a beautiful temple permanently in ISKCON's name worth at least $200,000."

About his trip to Australia, Rameśvara's upbeat assessment was in contrast to what Gurukṛpa told me the other day. Concerning Madhudviṣa's leaving there he said, "The rumors of a huge sum of laxmi missing have been proven false." As for the temples he said, "Melbourne and Sydney temples are very blissful, always absorbed in book distribution and just now organizing to make many new devotees. Eventually they are thinking to get a better building in Sydney, and to open restaurants in both cities. Gurukripa Swami and I spent 3 days together and he is in good spiritual mood, ready to execute all your orders as usual. His kirtan is still the strongest I have ever experienced. He has organized one traveling bus party in Australia to help make new devotees. If Gurukripa Swami spends more time in Australia then things can develop faster."

Śrīla Prabhupāda was very pleased and relieved by Rāmeśvara's report. Telling him his solution to amend the constitution was nice, he offered his own solution to the problem of local management. "Let Vasudeva become president. Your idea to sell BTGs, collect donations, hold kirtana and distribute prasada profusely, yes, do that. I was given the impression that this temple was to be controlled by the Punja family and our devotees would not have any hand. This was the impression given. We want that a very nice relationship be kept with Vasudeva. It was wanted that he follows our instructions including following the GBC, so that everything can go on nicely. Let one brother be president and one treasurer, and give one good man who can act as secretary. I have not lost confidence in Vasudeva. Now the matter is clear—I'm very much pleased with him so let him remain president and that will please him more, and his brother treasurer with one secretary. If the temple remains permanently in ISKCON Fiji's name and cannot be sold, that is very nice; it is not for selling, it is for improving more and more.

"Local men must understand our philosophy, then it will be very successful. We cannot import men from outside. We sincerely want that local men either from Vasudeva's family or any other family which will take on the work. We have to work on that line. Just like some of my Godbrothers wanted to take men from India to London but the attempt was a failure—but when I trained up local men then it was successful. I have no objection if the whole Vasudeva Punja family be trained up and take charge of the temple. Local men should not simply become a visitor but they should be trained up to take charge of the temple. That is what I want. As soon as one is a devotee there is no personal ambition—life is dedicated for Krishna.

"If my books can be translated and published there, I have no objection. Since Tamala and yourself are there for some time everything will be alright. Vasudeva must be president."

Having just discussed Gurukṛpa Mahārāja's service at length with him, Prabhupāda wrote to Rāmeśvara, "Gurukrpa is feeling inconvenience regarding Australia because of the long distance. His interest is mainly Japan. You or another man may take care of Australia."

\* \* \*

Śrīla Prabhupāda discussed the temple management again today with Hansadūta Mahārāja. He emphasized that the title of President or GBC was not important; there should be some substance to one's work. Recalling his own efforts to help establish the Gaudiya Math temple in Bombay in the early 1930s, Prabhupāda said, "I was living with servant and two sons. So I helped to start ... I took funds from my friends, I collected some money and ... So other important members said, 'Why Abhaya Babu is living separately? He should be the president of the Bombay.' I never said, but they said. I was living separately. Then Prabhupāda requested, I mean to say, pleaded in my behalf so many things. He said three words, 'It is better that he is living outside your company. He will do, when time will come, he'll do himself everything. You haven't got to recommend him.' These very words."

Prabhupāda told Hansadūta that Kṛṣṇa is simply giving a chance to everyone. He has no need of GBCs or temple presidents. "Otherwise thousands of presidents and thousands of GBC may come and go, His work will go on. Kṛṣṇa is complete Himself. He doesn't require anyone's help. That is Kṛṣṇa."

Prabhupāda stressed on preaching, quoting the famous saying of his spiritual master that a dead man cannot preach.

Hansadūta enthusiastically informed him that he had already deployed a German devotee, Ikṣvāku dāsa, to roam the temple grounds and greet visitors, show them around and sell them books. In the first few hours Ikṣvāku sold seventy rupees worth of books. Hansadūta said he thought that at least two or three life members could be made and hundreds of books sold each week without even having to leave the temple.

Prabhupāda agreed with him and said that last night he had noted many respectable gentlemen.

Hansadūta had also seen them. "Last night four people came, they were all big businessmen. One man had been working in a big business in Germany. He spoke German perfectly well. He was an Indian man, he lives in Agra. And so many people. Because Vṛndāvana is the heart of India, every Indian comes once in his lifetime to Vṛndāvana, if not more times. And everyone will come to our temple."

Prabhupāda smiled. "Due to Vṛndāvana, our temple is advertised all over India. Everyone says."

Prabhupāda was in a relaxed mood, interspersing his conversation with short *japa* breaks. He kept emphasizing that Hansadūta be practical and do something now to attract people to come, rather than simply project big ideas about what he could do in the future. He told a story of some servants who were given different services. "So one was to control horses. So he became very much anxious, 'What kind of whip I shall have to keep?'"

Hansadūta caught on quickly, "First he has to get a horse."

Prabhupāda nodded and shook with laughter. "Then, 'first of all, rascal, where is your horse?' He became very much anxious, 'What kind of whip?'"

Hansadūta smiled. "O.K. I'll get the horses."

"And anyone who can purchase a horse," Prabhupāda went on, "he can very easily purchase any whip. Not that we shall be very much anxious for the whip first. First of all, let us have a horse. The difficulty is that no horses coming, that is the difficulty. Attract horse, and you'll find so many."

\* \* \*

As I massaged Prabhupāda under his mosquito net on the roof tonight, he complained about the dogs barking and yowling in the alleyways. They were disturbing his sleep. He shook his head and told me that a birth as a dog is a most unfortunate situation. Because they are weak from hunger, they fight and yowl. But if you feed them, they become strong, and then they fight even more, making even more disturbance. He said there is no use in feeding them or in taking compassion on them. They are a condemned species, especially meant for starving and having a hard life.

He said there is nothing lower than a dog, yet even dogs have one good quality—faithfulness. And he told me a story about a man, a dog and a baby: The man had to leave his house for a few minutes, so he placed his baby on a bed and left his dog in the room to guard it. When he returned a short while later, the room was empty. He was horrified to find a trail of blood leading out into the garden. Following it, he suddenly came upon the dog running out from the bushes, its mouth covered in blood. The man was shocked. He thought that the dog must have attacked the baby, dragged it into the bushes and killed it. He angrily rushed inside, got a gun, and returned to face the dog. As he pointed the gun at the dog, the animal sat obediently before his master, making no attempt to run away. Bang! He killed the dog. But at the loud report of the gun, the cry of a baby rent the air. Confused, the man ran inside and found his child lying under the bed, unharmed. Now perplexed, the man retraced the trail of blood into the garden. Behind the bushes he found the body of a dead fox covered in blood. It was clear what had happened: The fox had threatened the baby, so the dog put the baby under the bed to protect it. It fought and killed the intruder and dragged it out into the garden. The man lamented his hasty action. The dog was so faithful that, although he knew he had fulfilled his duty in a valiant way, still he did not protest when his master shot him.

The conclusion, Śrīla Prabhupāda told me, is that the disciple should serve the spiritual master in the same way. If the disciple cannot remain faithful to his spiritual master, he is less than a dog.

## September 27th, 1976

Śrīla Prabhupāda explained in class this morning the duty of government. Interestingly, despite his many criticisms of the British, he used them as an example of good government. "So two *brahmāstra* weapons released, one by Aśvatthāmā and by Arjuna, it created havoc, catastrophe, and the people were suffering. So this is the duty of the government, to see that everyone is in peaceful condition. During Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira's time they were so happy that it is stated that there was not even scorching heat and pinching cold also, neither people were in anxiety for their livelihood. This is government: to see that people are in good atmosphere in everything, that is the first duty of the government. Of course, we have seen at the present moment also, in some of the European government they have got very good arrangement. In England I have seen, although they have lost their empire, still, people get free education, free medical treatment. And England does not produce practically anything except potato. They, the government imports so many eatables so that people may not suffer for want of food. So that is the way of good government from the time immemorial."

As he spoke Prabhupāda coughed and choked a little and asked for water. I reached over for the metal cup that sits by his side during every class. I removed the cover as I began to pass it over to him. Then I noticed that it was completely empty. Embarrassed, I had to send someone out to fill it. Śrīla Prabhupāda had just described how an expert king was so responsible that he even had to supply proper weather for his citizens, and here we were, failing to supply even one glass of water.

Prabhupāda shook his head in disgust at our mismanagement. "Hmm. Another rascal."

By the time the cup was returned, Prabhupāda was already back into his lecture. I vowed to add the cup to my list of things to check each morning. I see the cup everyday and have always assumed that the temple devotees were taking responsibility for filling it. Now I know better.

\* \* \*

Śrīla Prabhupāda has heard from Gopāla Kṛṣṇa prabhu at last. He had been delayed in Bombay on some BBT work and arrived in Delhi yesterday morning. However, it wasn't good news: He sent Prabhupāda a letter of resignation.

Gopāla said he had planned to come to Vṛndāvana but he has now changed his mind. He is under the impression that Śrīla Prabhupāda has made Hansadūta the GBC, and Tejīyas told him that Hansadūta is planning to take over the running of the Delhi temple as well. Feeling that Hansadūta has politically maneuvered his ousting, Gopāla said that he cannot face working with him.

Gopāla also expressed deep dissatisfaction with, and mistrust of, several of his *sannyāsī* godbrothers here in India. He confided in Prabhupāda that they were all working to undermine his efforts because he is a householder. He requested Prabhupāda to replace him as the GBC saying, "It would be better if a sannyasi is made GBC. My suggestion is: let Hansaduta be GBC for my whole zone and Mahamsa be his assistant."

He said he wanted to be honest with Śrīla Prabhupāda because he is his spiritual master and he understood that he is non-different from Kṛṣṇa. He offered two reasons why he could not continue. Firstly, he said he was certain that the *sannyāsīs* were spreading poison about him to turn other devotees against him. He said his mind was completely disturbed by "the political manner these devotees act to get power. So let them have power." Secondly he said, "I am a grihastha, so it is better that I leave the managing to the sannyasis. I have no plans or attraction to give up my family. Frankly, I am disappointed with the way 90% of ISKCON sannyasis act and behave."

He hoped that Śrīla Prabhupāda would relieve him of his GBC duties so that he could return to America, get a job and live with his family. "I want to live in a Krsna conscious way. Frankly I feel I was more Krsna conscious when I was living in the US than now as a GBC. I promise you I have no plans to leave your lotus feet. I am firmly convinced that only via you can I please the Supreme Lord and you are the only representative. I just want your blessings. Only with your blessings will I be able to serve the Supreme Lord."

Offering to work with Hansadūta for one month to ensure a smooth transition, he concluded, "I hope that I have not displeased you. My mind is so confused for the past several months. So I have placed my desire to be relieved to you and have also explained the reasons. No one is indispensable and I can guarantee that your movement in India will go on even better without me."

The letter confirmed Śrīla Prabhupāda's suspicions. It is yet another big headache for His Divine Grace. The fact is that Śrīla Prabhupāda is quite pleased with Gopāla Kṛṣṇa prabhu's efforts as GBC, and he does not want to lose his service. He wrote back a short reply with instructions that it be delivered immediately to Delhi: "Hansaduta is not GBC, you are GBC. No, don't return U.S. Immediately come here and talk with me. Don't do like rascal."

Dr. S. B. Chatterjee, the retired professor and head of department from North Bengal University and the University of Calcutta, who wrote to Prabhupāda while we were in Delhi, offering his services, sent another letter outlining a plan for training students in Vedic principles, Sanskrit studies and philosophy. He enquired whether Śrīla Prabhupāda was interested in such a scheme.

Prabhupāda replied positively, at least in principle. "I have no objection to your proposal and I can finance this proposal also. But I am afraid there will be hardly any students—that is the difficulty. I have seen in foreign countries that practically no students join high philosophical and scientific classes. People nowadays are only interested in money-earning philosophy. Nobody goes to the philosophical classes in universities. A similar institute was imagined by my Godbrother Bon Maharaj in Vrindaban, but it has not become very successful. There are many difficulties in the line, but I like the idea; therefore if some practical solution can be made we can discuss personally, but I appreciate your idea. The only difficulty I'm feeling is whether we can get sufficient students. Some of my disciples who are Ph.D.'s in science, they are also attempting our institution in Boston U.S.A., but I'm still doubtful how far they'll be successful on account of scarcity of students. It is said in the Kali-yuga every man is on the standard of sudra, and the curriculum suggested by you is meant for the brahmana—that is the difficulty.

"We are attempting one Gurukula in Vrindaban and we have already begun building, to train children from the very beginning of life as is advised by Prahlad Maharaj:

*kaumara acaret prajno*  
*dharman bhagavatan iha*  
*durlabham manusam janma*  
*tad apy adhruvam arthadam (Bhag.* [*7.6.1*](https://vedarama.com/en/books/sb-7/6.1)*)*

"But there is also difficulty of getting students because the parents and the guardians are not interested. Before going to America I approached many respectable friends for giving me at least one boy from each family to be trained up in this line of self-realization, but I was not successful. The parents had no interest—the same difficulty of sudra mentality. Anyway, we are attempting again this Gurukula program, so why not begin from this small endeavor and gradually develop to the ideal university. On the whole if you can arrange such university there will be no financial difficulty. So I think if you kindly begin from this Gurukula attempt and then develop to the International University, that will be very practical.

"Of course we have to have independent private university because the government is not interested according to Vedic ideology. Bon Maharaj tried for the last forty years to make a vaishnava university recognised by the government, but he failed."

Prabhupāda added that he would inform Dr. Chatterjee when he comes to Calcutta so that they can meet.

Śrīla Prabhupāda also received a letter from Sharma dāsa, the black American devotee who was preaching in Africa last year, but left to go and sit in Māyāpur and chant 150 rounds a day. In February, prior to the Gaura Pūrṇimā festival, he asked Prabhupāda if he could build a tree house because he was disturbed by devotees coming to see him. Then again in March, he asked if he could go to Rādhā-kuṇḍa and chant because his *bhajana* was being disturbed by visits from his Godbrothers. Prabhupāda had told him that his disturbed mind meant that he was not fit for only chanting. Prabhupāda had been pleased when Sharma decided that he return to Africa and preach. But now, in his letter sent from Nairobi, he again requested permission to make chanting his main service. Saying that he didn't want to act whimsically and that he only wanted to please Śrīla Prabhupāda, he declared, "We have no love for Kṛṣṇa but we have this attraction to serve Kṛṣṇa as a servant of the confidential serving maids of Kṛṣṇa. By your mercy we understand that we cannot go to Vṛndāvana by any ticket so we are by the grace of Kṛṣṇa trying to fix our mind on this service in Vṛndāvana. This fixing of the mind is dependant on my chanting Kṛṣṇa names, and my chanting Kṛṣṇa names is simply dependant on your mercy because my Godbrothers do not like me chanting. We do not want to commit offences to our godbrothers yet sometimes when I tell them I only want to hear about Kṛṣṇa in Vṛndāvana or the glories of His holy name or qualities, some say we must talk of other things. They are more pure than my sinful self. As far as this living entity, he only wants to hear or talk of Kṛṣṇa. My Godbrothers as far as I am concerned are better and more advanced, but because of my sinful condition if you would allow me to chant these few extra rounds, read your books and render some small service, maybe before leaving this body Kṛṣṇa will allow this sinful living entity to be elevated to the position of one of His loving servants. It is our only desire to have our devotional creeper take shelter of Goloka Vṛndāvana and to somehow or other please our spiritual master and Kṛṣṇa."

Śrīla Prabhupāda's reply was to him was quite terse: "So, why did you leave Mayapur if you are so expert in chanting? Read my books and do some menial service, but why you have left Mayapur? You are restless, so what can be done. You were chanting in Mayapur. Wherever you may live, you have to abide by the order of the authority. Because you are restless you are not fit for chanting absolutely."

## September 28th, 1976

Prabhupāda is still not going out for a morning walk. He is not feeling strong and his health problems persist.

\* \* \*

From the *Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam* this morning, we heard how Kṛṣṇa advised Arjuna not to be merciful to Aśvatthāmā even though he was the son of an exalted *brāhmaṇa*. Śrīla Prabhupāda has often said that one's birth status is not an indication of one's qualification. Today he offered an explanation of this that I haven't heard before. "Everyone can say, 'I am the son of a *brāhmaṇa*.' That is *brahma-bandhu*, or a friend of a *brāhmaṇa*. That does not mean he is a *brāhmaṇa*. This is the idea—*brāhmaṇa* is not the body, *brāhmaṇa* is the quality. If the *brāhmaṇa* is body, then when a *brāhmaṇa* is dead, the sons take the dead body to the crematorium place and burn the body. Then if the body is *brāhmaṇa*, then the sons are committing sins by *brahma-hatyā*. No; that is not *brahma-hatyā-brāhmaṇa* is the quality. With the departure of the soul, that quality is gone. Now this body is simply a lump of matter, so there is no shame when the body is burnt into ashes.

"So in considering all angles of vision," he said, "this Aśvatthāmā was not a *brāhmaṇa*. Therefore Kṛṣṇa personally advised him, *mā enaṁ pārtha arhasi trātum*: 'Don't excuse him. Kill him, this *brahma-bandhu*. He has done wrong, now he deserves to be killed.' It is clearly said, so does it mean that Kṛṣṇa is advising *brahma-hatyā*? No. Kṛṣṇa cannot do that. He is the teacher, world teacher. How He can advise somebody, especially His friend Arjuna? *Bhakto 'si priyo 'si me*. Can you advise anything adversely to your friend? To your son? No, I must give very good advice. So Kṛṣṇa is advising Arjuna, 'Don't excuse this rascal *brahma-bandhu*. Don't excuse.'"

Prabhupāda added that although this was Kṛṣṇa's strong advice it did not mean that we could take advantage and do anything and everything under the pretext of it being Kṛṣṇa's advice. "You must be first of all a confidential friend or servant of Kṛṣṇa, you must receive direct order from Kṛṣṇa. Then you can do it, otherwise not. Otherwise not. Under the pretext that 'Kṛṣṇa said,' 'My spiritual master has said,' 'Prabhupāda has said,' we manufacture something. Don't do that. Unless you are directly ordered, you cannot do, at least such things as to chastise a *brahma-bandhu*. This should not be done. Here is direct order."

Another point Prabhupāda made was that good government can only come from trained *kṣatriyas*, not from the lower, uncultured class of man. "It is said in the *Bhāgavatam* there was no anxiety. The citizens should feel so much safe, that 'We have such a nice king that we have no danger at all. Not being injured, not our property being stolen or injustice given.' That is the real government—when the citizens will feel completely safe. That requires *kṣatriya*. Not these *cāmāra*, *bhangis*, and *śūdras* voted and become the president and minister—that will not be successful. That is not possible. There must be trained-up *kṣatriyas*, then there will be good government. Trained. They should be trained means they should be advised by the *brāhmaṇas*. Therefore four divisions required."

\* \* \*

This morning Prabhupāda received a letter from Harikeśa Swami, who is still in Delhi. Written yesterday, it was a humble plea. He said that he has a serious case of malaria, and might even die. Therefore he begged forgiveness for his offences, both against Prabhupāda and also against me.

When I read it out to Prabhupāda he looked at me and shook his head in innocent surprise. "I did not think he was creating any offence." I was also surprised that Harikeśa felt he had offended me, and I was embarrassed to be mentioned in the same frame as Śrīla Prabhupāda.

The letter invoked Prabhupāda's compassion and he wrote back: "I am very much perturbed to hear you are suffering from malaria in Delhi. So don't be worried, you'll very soon recover, but I think it is a hindrance for you going to Europe. I therefore request you not to proceed to Europe immediately, but stay and recoup your health, and then we shall think over your going abroad. In the meantime deposit the money in my account at State Bank of India, Connaught Place. Tejiyas knows the bank and he will do the needful. Hoping for your speedy recovery."

A bit perplexed by his suggestion that Harikeśa not go to Europe, I asked Prabhupāda why he said that. He clarified his thoughts. "It appears these hindrances mean that perhaps God does not want him to go to Europe, so better wait for some time and then decide."

Jayapatāka Swami sent a long report on his preaching in Bengal. Since seeing Śrīla Prabhupāda in Hyderabad he said many things have happened. Two newspapers, one of them put out by the Communist Party of India, recently printed defamatory articles about us. Although they do not enjoy wide circulation, Jayapatāka felt that some appropriate legal action should be taken against them, lest people start to believe their false claims. To counter them He is endeavoring to present favorable articles, especially from our preaching in the West, to other newspapers and he was especially thankful to Śrīla Prabhupāda for sending various news clippings from his recent tour, which he said, proved especially useful in preaching to government officials.

He presented news on a number of other issues: The Haridaspur land is now in ISKCON's name, except for a small portion which requires signing over by some people in Calcutta, but he does not envision any problem with this. He wants Saurabha prabhu to design the Haridaspur temple before he begins collecting funds for the project, but in the meantime he requested money to build a boundary wall. Jayapatāka asked about the Deities for the new temple. Although Prabhupāda had previously suggested installing Gaura-Nitāi, some locals have asked for Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, and Jayapatāka also asked if a *mūrti* of Ṭhākura Haridāsa should be installed. Jayapatāka was still optimistic about our application for land acquisition in Māyāpur. The Chief Secretary has written to him asking for a full proposal for our plans throughout W. Bengal and he asked for Prabhupāda's advice on what to write. Jayapatāka Mahārāja apologized for disturbing Śrīla Prabhupāda with his questions, but said he felt that they were not ordinary. "They are unique projects of your Divine Grace, therefore without your direction it is difficult to carry forward. I hope that I am not disturbing your translation for which we are all eagerly grateful."

In other bits of news he said the construction on the new long building was going ahead, but at reduced pace, with 150 workers striving to complete it before Śrīla Prabhupāda's expected arrival in late autumn. Electrical and plumbing works would begin when they receive a promised ten *lakhs* from Gurukṛpa Mahārāja's party. New devotees are joining, handloom production has increased, and people are still attending our free *prasādam* distribution. He also said that the Ganges was flooding in some areas, and he suggested that we could purchase some vans to be used as mobile cooking and distribution centers, which, when not attending emergencies, could be used for preaching programs and propaganda work.

He briefly mentioned that Śatadhanya Mahārāja's visa problems were the same as Bhavānanda's. He had only a tourist visa and would have to leave and re-enter.

Finally, he gave news about their efforts to produce Bengali books. They have received one issue of *Bhagavat Darshana*, but it was printed on letterpress and was not up to our standards. Therefore he is planning to print the next one by offset press. "Sales are good, people are interested. If a good leader would come then I could give him the boat to take out as we have a crew, but no sufficient leaders. However we are looking. In the meantime distribution is going on in the main cities by train."

Prabhupāda heard the entire lengthy report carefully, and answered each point thoroughly. "Regarding the Haridaspur land, first give the site plan and boundary statement and then we shall make plan with Saurabh. Yes, Gaur-Nitai Deities can be installed firstly as we generally do, also Lord Jagannath and then Radha-Krishna, in three compartments ... Thakur Haridas's murti can be installed.

"Regarding our proposal for West Bengal: West Bengal people may come and join us without any distinction of caste and creed. The occupation will be according to one's capacity.
